Full text appears complete. Given these points, I include this study in the meta-analysis.

The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete.

Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that implements a perceptual decision-making task (visual random-dot-motion lotteries) where subjects estimate probability of correct perceptual judgments and choose between lotteries. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (mixed-effects FLAME) with cluster correction and presents contrasts/parametric effects for reward probability, reward value, and expected value (within-task, condition-wise parametric contrasts), satisfying condition-versus-condition/task-versus-control forms required. Participants are healthy adults and whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic (risky) monetary decision-making task. The paper reports within-task contrasts and parametric correlations (EV vs RM, TD error, uncertainty) and conjunction analyses—i.e., condition-versus-condition effects rather than task>rest. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain/random-effects SPM results with voxelwise statistics and reported peak coordinates (with whole-brain and SVC corrections). Participants are healthy adults. Results and coordinates are fully reported in the main text and figures. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, rest-baseline-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Stoplight driving game). It reports within-task contrasts directly comparing decision conditions (Go > Stop) and outcome contrasts (Pass > Crash), and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected) with reported peak coordinates. Participants are healthy humans and whole-brain results are clearly described. No exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study tests decision-making processes (probabilistic and risk mechanisms) during pronoun reference resolution, directly manipulating uncertainty and risk. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5 second-level random-effects) with condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., Undetermined > Directly Determined; Indirectly Determined > Directly Determined) and a parametric uncertainty analysis (high > low uncertainty). Participants are healthy adults. Results are reported with whole-brain coordinates and corrected thresholds. Thus it meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI of risky/ambiguous decision-making, includes appropriate contrasts, provides whole-brain group maps, and involves an eligible participant group. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (e.g., task>rest-only contrasts, PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a multi-attribute decision-making task where trials systematically varied the variability (ambiguity) of value predictions. The authors explicitly decoded variability (sorted into four groups) and tested where in the brain variability/ambiguity information was represented, performing group-level, voxelwise second-level statistics on whole-brain searchlight accuracy maps and reporting MNI coordinates. This constitutes a condition-vs-condition (high vs low variability/ambiguity) analysis appropriate for ambiguous decision-making contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and reports whole-brain coordinates, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human older adults performing a lottery choice task that manipulates risk via probabilities and magnitudes (risky decision-making). The authors report within-task contrasts using parametric modulators of expected value (EV) and group-level voxelwise analyses identifying positive and negative EV sensitivity, age and risk-preference effects, and feedback-related contrasts; results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps with peak-voxel tables and figures. These analyses satisfy the requirement for condition-vs-condition/task contrasts (e.g., sensitivity to high vs low EV/riskier vs surer) and provide group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation evidence. The task and sample fall within eligible participant groups. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not rest-baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study of probabilistic reversal learning (decision-making under uncertainty) in healthy human participants using within-task contrasts (shift>stay for choice under uncertainty; reward>punishment for outcome). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (TFCE, permutation-corrected) and also ROI follow-ups; whole-brain results are described in text, figures, and tables. The shift>stay contrast explicitly models decisional processes under high uncertainty (post-PE and post-reversal trials), which maps onto the review's ambiguous/risky decision-making domain. Participants are healthy adults, and the full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this fMRI study clearly scanned human participants during a risky decision-making task and reports group-level whole-brain contrasts and coordinates, it does not report any qualified decision-making contrast of the types required by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, risk > certainty, ambiguity > non-ambiguity, or perceptual hard > easy). The reported neuroimaging contrasts focus on incidental CS cue processing (Touched_CS > Shocked_CS; Shocked_CS > Touched_CS) prior to gamble presentation rather than contrasts that directly compare decision-making conditions (e.g., risky vs safe choices or task vs control). Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (fMRI during risky decision task), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria from the provided list apply. Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a probabilistic decision-making task that manipulates risk. The authors modelled trial-by-trial risk prediction and used GLM parametric regressors to produce group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (cluster- and voxel-level corrected) identifying regions correlating with risk prediction; they report and correlate these maps with behavior and personality. Thus the study meets I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric modulation indexing risk prediction across conditions), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not ROI-only; not resting-state-only; not task>rest only). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in which healthy human participants performed the Balloon Analog Risk Task (a risky decision-making task) during BOLD scanning. Analyses include within-subject, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (e.g., active choice > passive choice, parametric risk-related contrasts, outcome contrasts) using SPM8 and random-effects ANOVAs, with cluster-corrected results reported. The passive no-choice condition serves as an active control compared with the active risky decision condition. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI risky decision-making studies and provides whole-brain activation evidence suitable for inclusion.

This fMRI study used the BIAS financial decision-making task (stocks vs bond) manipulating uncertainty/risk and measured BOLD while participants made choices. It reports task contrasts relevant to the review (neural representation of uncertainty as a parametric modulation, and comparisons preceding bond vs stock choices — i.e., risk-avoidant vs risk-seeking), at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise analyses (reported clusters, tables/figures). Participants include clinical (violent offenders subgroups) and healthy controls, which is acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (with tables/figures referenced). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening.

This study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: it acquired task-based fMRI while participants performed a risky decision-making task (incidental emotion regulation followed by a risky vs safe choice task). The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts using SPM (e.g., Risky Choices > Safe Choices) thresholded at p<0.05 FWE and provide coordinate results and second-level analyses. The full text includes methods, GLMs, and whole-brain fMRI results, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical whole-brain fMRI study in humans using a probabilistic object reversal task with explicit decision-making under uncertainty (probabilistic rewards). The authors report within-group and between-group voxelwise contrasts for decision-making ("learned" vs "search") and reward processing using SPM2 and provide coordinate tables and figures. The task involves probabilistic outcomes (80% vs 20%), which qualifies as risky/ambiguous decision-making. There is at least one within-task decision-making contrast (Decision making: learned vs search). Whole-brain group-level maps are reported. Participants are healthy human adults. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-group task contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision task (face/house discrimination) with concurrent metacognitive (confidence) reports. It includes a within-task condition contrast (Report > Follow) that contrasts an active metacognitive report vs a yoked control, which constitutes a task-versus-control comparison relevant to perceptual decision-making. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with corrected clusters and tabulated coordinates. Participants and methods are fully described and the full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing the Balloon Analog Risk Task (a risky decision-making paradigm). It includes within-task contrasts comparing risky versus non-risk (mean color pump > mean white pump), parametric (linear color > linear white) contrasts of risk level, and outcome contrasts (Explosions > Cashouts), all analyzed at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction. Participants (heavy drinkers) are an acceptable group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing risky decision-making tasks (choices between risky and safe options). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe and high-risk versus low-risk conditions, and uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results and peak coordinates reported. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for risky decision-making fMRI contrasts and whole-brain activation reporting, and does not violate any exclusion criteria (not PET, not resting/seed-only, not ROI-only, and includes within-group task contrasts).

This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses. The GLM includes condition contrasts (active pumps vs control pumps, parametric modulation by pump number, and pumps following cash-out vs explosion), and results are reported as whole-brain maps and region lists. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making and provides the necessary whole-brain contrasts and reporting.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a canonical risky decision-making task (Risky Gains). The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing risky versus safe responses and punished versus non-punished outcomes, and presents both a-priori ROI and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (with cluster correction), with results described in text, tables, and figures. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky decision-making and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in humans using a risky decision-making task (modified Balloon Analog Risk Task) with both active (choice) and passive (no-choice) conditions. It includes within- and between-task contrasts (e.g., active risk vs. passive risk; active inflation vs. passive inflation; active loss vs. passive loss) that directly compare decision-making conditions. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects GLM results (normalized to MNI space, reported with whole-brain FDR-corrected thresholds and cluster tables), and results are presented in figures and tables. Participants are healthy humans. The full text contains introduction, methods, results and discussion, so the report is complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study in human youth performing a well-established risky decision-making task (Cups Task) during scanning, reporting within-task contrasts (risky vs nonrisky; gain vs loss) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (FLAME1, cluster-corrected). The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets the meta-analysis scope (risky decision-making) and all required inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The study is excluded because its decision task is value-based (pleasantness/reward) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review (exclusion E5). The paper reports fMRI in humans and contains appropriate contrasts and whole-brain group maps, but the domain of the decision (judging pleasantness of odors / reward-based choice) does not match the meta-analysis target domains. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (within-task contrasts: correct vs error, decision vs rating; ΔI regressors), I6 (group-level whole-brain SPM analyses with coordinates reported), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results/coordinates reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task per the meta-analysis scope). No other exclusion criteria applied. Confidence reflects clear domain mismatch based on full text.

This is an fMRI study using a risky decision-making task (modified cups task) performed by human participants (I4). The paper reports relevant within-task contrasts (risky > sure / risky–sure and related target×situation×choice contrasts) that match the admissible risky-DM contrasts (I5). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results reported with whole-brain FWE correction and coordinate information (I6, I8). Participants are healthy young adults (I7). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-task contrasts vs rest, or non-decision tasks) are met. Therefore the study should be included.

The study reports an fMRI experiment (BART) administered during scanning (risky decision-making), satisfying I4. It includes explicit condition-vs-control contrasts (Active Pumpsparametric vs Control Pumpsparametric; Active vs Control), satisfying I5. Analyses are whole-brain GLM with voxelwise thresholding and cluster correction and report coordinates and group-level results, satisfying I6 and I8. Participants are healthy adult males (eligible under I7). No exclusion criteria are met: it is not PET (E4), not ROI-only (E6), not connectivity-only (E7) and contrasts are condition-vs-control rather than task>rest (not E3). Full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and references, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Overall, all required inclusion criteria (I4,I5,I6,I7,I8) are met and no exclusion criteria apply, so the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study in humans using a gambling task that manipulates reward uncertainty (uncertain, probable, certain) during decision-making, i.e., a risky/ambiguous decision-making paradigm. The paper reports within-task, condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., uncertain wins > probable wins; probable wins > probable losses) and examines outcome effects (wins vs losses). Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (t-to-z maps, exploratory whole-brain contrasts) and ROI definitions derived from whole-brain contrasts. Participants were healthy adults. Thus the study meets I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous DM), I5 (condition contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/analyses). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not only task>rest contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). Full text is complete.

This is a whole-brain fMRI study in human smokers using the Wheel of Fortune, a probabilistic (risky) decision-making task. The paper reports task-versus-control contrasts (money > control) during selection and anticipation phases and win>no-win during outcome, modeled and reported at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-corrected maps and coordinate tables/figures). Participant group (nicotine-dependent smokers) is acceptable. Reporting includes coordinates, tables and figures. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are against an active control (not implicit baseline), not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not only between-group contrasts without within-task effects. Full text is complete.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that manipulated reward probability (risk) within an economic decision task and analyzed task-evoked BOLD responses. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM) with task-versus-control contrasts (DM > C2) and regression analyses using entropy; results are reported as clusters/coordinates. Participants are healthy adults. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision task), I5 (decision task vs active control contrasts reported), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study reports fMRI in human participants performing a probability (risk) discounting task (probabilistic rewards) and a delay discounting task. The probability discounting task constitutes a risky decision-making paradigm. The main reported contrasts include free vs. forced choice (decision vs. an active, matched control), meeting the requirement for a task-versus-control contrast. Analyses were whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise (SPM; coordinates and FWE-corrected results reported), and results are reported as coordinates and figures. Participants include clinical and non-clinical groups (allowed). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical human fMRI study that directly investigates risky financial decision-making (BIAS task) during event-related fMRI with group-level whole-brain analyses. The manuscript reports voxelwise group maps and condition contrasts (e.g., stock gain > loss, market relative gain > loss, stock vs bond choice) with thresholding and Talairach coordinates, and also describes prediction analyses relating anticipatory activation to subsequent risky vs riskless choices. Participants are healthy volunteers. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, fMRI acquisition, analysis), Results, and Discussion; supplemental material is referenced. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only).

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reversal learning task that involves decision making under uncertainty (probabilistic reward contingencies and reversals), matching the review's focus on risky/ambiguous decision-making. fMRI was recorded while participants performed the task (I4). The authors report within-task model-derived contrasts (reward prediction error as a parametric modulator at feedback) and group-level comparisons (including main effects of RPE and OCD>control contrasts), satisfying the requirement for at least one decision-making contrast (I5) and providing whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps (cluster-corrected) suitable for meta-analysis (I6). Participant groups (patients and healthy controls) are acceptable (I7). Results are reported in-text and in supplementary figures/tables (I8). The study does not violate exclusion criteria: it is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in which human adolescents performed a risky decision-making task (Yellow Light Game) in the scanner (meets I4). The paper reports within-task, condition-vs-condition contrasts involving decision types (go=risky and stop=safe) across social contexts (peer vs parent), i.e., comparisons of decision-making conditions (meets I5). Analyses were group-level, whole-brain random-effects maps with cluster correction and results shared on NeuroVault (meets I6 and I8). Participant sample falls within acceptable ages and groups (meets I7). No exclusion criteria are triggered: the study does not rely solely on baseline contrasts, is not PET, reports whole-brain task activation (not ROI-only), and includes task contrasts beyond seed-based connectivity (so E3,E4,E6,E7,E8,E9 do not apply). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI risky decision-making.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making (gambling) task. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., decisions after Norisk vs Riskwin; Risk vs Norisk; RA > FG > RD) and analyzes decision-related and feedback-related BOLD responses. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-corrected, GRFT) with MNI coordinates and tables; ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain results are present. The participants are healthy adults and results are clearly described in methods, results and discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study in human participants performing the risky-gains task (risky decision-making). The authors report within-task contrasts (risky > safe) at the subject level and group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses (SPM2 t-maps with voxel-wise threshold and cluster extent), and present activation tables/figures. Participants are healthy human adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making (risky > safe) with whole-brain group maps; no exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, baseline-only contrasts, ROI-only reporting) are met.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing an ambiguous decision-making task (ambiguous cue conditioning) with explicit choices (obtain reward vs avoid punishment). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8) including condition contrasts (positive tone vs negative tone) and parametric modulations across tones (linear and quadratic effects indexing valence generalization and ambiguity). Results are reported as whole-brain maps and tables with cluster-level FWE correction. Participants and task fall squarely within the ambiguous decision-making domain. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET-only, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts) apply. Full text is complete.

This study meets the review’s inclusion criteria: (I4) it collected fMRI data while human adolescents performed a risky decision-making task (BART); (I5) it reports condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to risky DM (Pumps > Control (color pumps vs. white control pumps), Cash Outs contrasts); (I6) group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-corrected thresholds and coordinates; (I7) participant group (healthy adolescents from Mexican backgrounds) is acceptable; (I8) whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and contrasts include task-versus-control rather than only implicit baseline. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore include for meta-analysis of fMRI risky decision-making.

Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a probabilistic/uncertainty feedback task that involves anticipation of gains/losses), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the study does not report any qualifying decision-making contrast of the forms required (e.g., risky > safe, high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty, hard > easy). The main reported contrasts are valence-based (gain vs loss anticipation; gain vs loss outcomes) rather than risk/ambiguity or perceptual difficulty contrasts (no bivalent > non-bivalent or analogous ambiguity contrasts are reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to meet I5 (required contrast specification) despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study in humans that explicitly examined risky decision-making using a lottery choice task (risk manipulated via coefficient of variation). The fMRI analysis included a group-level whole-brain analysis testing how CV for chosen gambles modulated BOLD during the decision phase (reporting higher vs lower risk effects in bilateral anterior insula with FWE correction), which constitutes condition-vs-condition/riskier>safer contrasts (parametric modulation). Participants are human adolescents (eligible by I7). Whole-brain results and coordinates/ROIs are described. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making and whole-brain group-level contrasts.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans performing a risky decision-making (gambling-like) task during whole-brain fMRI. The paper reports within-task condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., Risk_DisAdv > Risk_Adv, Risk_DisAdv_Win > Risk_Adv_Win, Risk_DisAdv_Lose > Risk_Adv_Lose) at the group level using voxelwise GLM and cluster-level correction, and presents regional results and figures/tables. The methods, results, and discussion are present (full text provided). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making whole-brain contrasts.

This study used fMRI while participants performed a risky decision-making task (50:50 monetary gambles), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with coordinate tables; participants are an acceptable sample and results are reported with coordinates. Therefore inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I6 (whole-brain group voxelwise analysis), I7 (acceptable participant group), I8 (coordinates/figures reported). However, the imaging results do not report a contrast that directly compares decision-making conditions (e.g., risky > safe, accept > reject, high-risk > low-risk) or an experimental risk task > control task. The primary reported contrast is novel > familiar prime and regressions of that contrast with subsequent risk-taking behavior; no within-task decision-making contrast (risky vs safe) is provided in the reported whole-brain results. Thus inclusion criterion I5 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because I5 is not met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a risky decision-making paradigm. The analyses include a parametric contrast indexing risk level (brain activation that covaried with parametric risk), which serves as a within-task risky > safe / high-risk > low-risk type contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise one-sample t-tests and statistical maps are reported for the risk, win, and loss contrasts. Participants are healthy adults. The paper therefore meets the meta-analysis requirements: (I4) fMRI during a risky decision-making task, (I5) a decision-related contrast (parametric risk level/high-risk > low-risk), (I6) group-level whole-brain voxelwise results, (I7) acceptable participant group, and (I8) whole-brain results described in the text/figures. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an fMRI experiment (BART) involving risky decision making in human participants, with within-task contrasts distinguishing risky versus safe choices and parametric modulators (e.g., ChooseInflate*P(explode), ChooseWin*P(explode)) and planned contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (with FDR and cluster correction) including coordinate tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, resting-state-only, task>rest-only contrasts, non-empirical) are met.

This study reports fMRI data collected while human participants performed a risky decision-making task (monetary lotteries). The authors present within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe choices (behavioral and BOLD contrasts) and examine modulation by regulation (Look vs Relax). Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLMs with FDR thresholding and tables/coordinates of regions (e.g., Table 2), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies (I4–I8) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This paper reports an fMRI study in humans performing a modified Iowa Gambling Task (a risky/uncertain decision-making task), and analyzes trial-to-trial prediction-error as a parametric regressor (a within-task contrast). The manuscript includes whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses (two-sample t tests with cluster correction) and reports within-group one-sample effects of the prediction-error regressor. Thus it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (within-task contrast: prediction-error parametric modulation), I6 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria appear to apply (not PET, not task>rest only, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Balloon Analogue Risk Task), includes condition-vs-control contrasts (mean pump events vs control-balloon events) and parametric modulation contrasts (risk/reward indexed by pump number), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster-corrected whole-brain analyses). Participant groups (methamphetamine users and healthy controls) are acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and limitations, so appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports an fMRI experiment using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a canonical risky decision-making task, with participants scanned while performing active-choice and passive-no-choice conditions. It presents within-task risk-level contrasts (parametric modulation of probability of explosion; effectively high-risk > low-risk comparisons) and an active-choice vs passive-no-choice contrast. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise, with multiple-comparison cluster correction; results are reported as clusters/coordinates and figures. Participants are human young adults (twins), and whole-brain task activation maps are described and used for voxelwise genetic modeling. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of human decision making under known probabilistic uncertainty (70% vs 30%) using a two-choice prediction task, meeting the meta-analysis focus on risky/uncertain decision-making. The experiment includes an active control task and reports within-task contrasts (prediction > control) for both age groups and group comparisons. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM5 results with corrected thresholds and coordinate tables/figures, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain evidence. Participants are healthy human adults. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, tables, figures, and discussion, so the report is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI study in humans of risky decision making using mixed gambles and choices (P_max, G_max, L_min). The paper reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., P_max > magnitude-sensitive choices; G_max vs L_min) and uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME, cluster-corrected maps). Participants are healthy young adults. Results include whole-brain activation maps and ROI/ connectivity analyses reported in text and supplemental materials. The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making with whole-brain contrasts and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans (n=8) that directly tests decision making under uncertainty (probabilistic reasoning tasks: balls-in-a-bottle and personality survey). It reports a condition-vs-condition contrast comparing decision making under uncertainty to decision making under certainty (ambiguous > non-ambiguous), using whole-brain, voxelwise group-level SPM analyses with corrected voxelwise statistics and tables/figures of coordinates. Participants are healthy; results are reported in figures and a coordinate table. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and references and appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of ambiguous decision-making and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a sequential foraging task with probabilistic (risky) outcomes. It meets inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task with probabilistic/risky choices), I5 (within-task contrasts/parametric effects comparing foraging vs waiting and value differences between choice options), I6 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses reported with FWE correction and maps available), I7 (healthy participant sample), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables; supplementary data shared). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only, and contains within-task contrasts rather than only between-group effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The study used fMRI while human participants performed a risky decision-making task (Risky Gains Task) and reports task contrasts directly comparing decision conditions (safe vs. risky; losses vs. wins; safe vs. risky following a loss). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM12 with one-sample (within-group) and two-sample (between-group) t-tests and cluster-level correction (AlphaSim), and task-evoked whole-brain activation maps were generated and used for reporting peak activations and correlations with behavior. Participants are human adults (women with obesity and healthy controls). Thus the paper meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and does not violate any listed exclusion criteria (no PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, includes within-group maps). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study where participants performed a risky decision-making task (risky-gains). The paper reports a within-task contrast comparing risky > safe choices (GLT risky vs safe) and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (linear mixed effects and robust regressions) with cluster-corrected results and region descriptions. Participants include HIV+ and seronegative controls (acceptable per criteria). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest-only, and includes within-group task effects). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that measured BOLD responses while subjects performed a perceptual decision-making task under ambiguity (face emotion morph judgments). The authors report within-task contrasts comparing ambiguity levels (e.g., increasing ambiguity and decreasing ambiguity effects) and identify whole-brain group-level activations using SPM random-effects analyses. Thus the paper provides eligible ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts (ambiguous > non-ambiguous and related contrasts) and whole-brain voxelwise results. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, not only baseline contrasts, and not non-empirical). Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

The full text reports an fMRI study in human participants performing a monetary decision-making task varying reward probability and magnitude (uncertainty/risk), satisfying I4. The authors report within-task contrasts modeling reward uncertainty (e.g., 50% vs 100%), reward magnitude and value, and prediction error contrasts, satisfying I5. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM second-level analyses with FDR/FWE correction and coordinate tables, satisfying I6 and I8. Participants are healthy adults, satisfying I7. The manuscript includes full introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants using a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion) with an active control task (arrows). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (AFNI 3dANOVA3, cluster-corrected maps) and provide cluster tables/coordinates. The key contrast (dots task > arrows control) and ramp-vs-down-ramp interaction test perceptual evidence accumulation (perceptual task > control task and task-related ramping). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study does not meet key inclusion requirements for the meta-analysis. While it uses fMRI and reports group-level whole-brain task activation maps (I6) and includes a healthy participant sample (I7), and presents whole-brain results/coordinates in text (I8), the critical decision-making manipulation (valence ratings of surprised faces) was performed outside the scanner. In the MRI session participants freely viewed faces (passive viewing) and performed an emotion regulation task (reappraise vs maintain), which is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during a decision-making task) and I5 (at least one decision-making contrast comparing decision conditions or task vs control) are not satisfied. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the study’s in-scanner tasks are not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks. Consequently the study must be excluded.

The study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses with no clear unmasked, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-activation maps required by inclusion criterion I6. This meets exclusion criterion E6. The paper does satisfy several inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I5 (contains risky > safe contrasts), I7 (healthy participants included), and I8 (results described in text/figures). However it does NOT provide the required whole-brain group-level voxelwise results (I6), so it cannot be included. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports task-based fMRI collected while human participants performed a risky decision-making task (CUPS) and includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (risky vs non-risky and parametric modulators of risk and reward). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (FLAME random-effects, cluster-corrected maps, tables/figures with coordinates). Participants include casual methamphetamine users and non-users, which is acceptable per study population criteria. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and not task>baseline only). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study in humans performing the Iowa Gambling Task, which assesses risky/ambiguous decision-making. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM2) and provides contrasts comparing decision-making vs an active control task and choices from risky versus safe decks (risky > safe), with coordinates and cluster statistics. Participants were healthy adult males. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study (n=5) of perceptual decision making using a dot-motion/color coherence task. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses testing parametric contrasts of coherence (i.e., low vs high coherence / hard > easy comparisons) and presents statistical maps, tables, and ROI analyses. The task and contrasts directly match perceptual decision-making criteria (parameterized motion/color coherence; attended vs ignored conditions). The paper provides full methods, results, and discussion (introduction, materials and methods, results, modeling, connectivity, discussion), so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (this is not PET; contrasts are condition-vs-condition parametric, not only baseline; whole-brain results are reported; not ROI-only or connectivity-only). Therefore the study meets inclusion for meta-analysis of fMRI perceptual decision-making.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a gambling (Blackjack) task that manipulates risk. It reports within-task contrasts directly comparing decision conditions (e.g., high-risk hits > low-risk hits; low-risk sits > high-risk sits) matching risky-DM contrast forms. Analyses used group-level, random-effects, voxelwise statistics and report Talairach coordinates and whole-brain/exploratory activations (tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Participants are an eligible group (healthy students). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI, task>rest contrasts only) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of fMRI risky decision-making.

This study reports fMRI in human participants performing a probabilistic reversal-learning task with stochastic rewards (decision-making under uncertainty/risk). It includes within-task contrasts and model-based regressors that compare decision conditions (e.g., switch > stay, prior-correct/value contrasts, and direct model comparisons state-based vs RL). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise maps with reported peak coordinates and thresholding, satisfying the meta-analysis reporting requirements. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state, and contrasts are condition-versus-condition rather than task>implicit baseline). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky/uncertain decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study of risky decision-making using a two-choice gambling task (Cake Gambling Task) with human participants. The paper reports within-task condition contrasts (High-Risk > Low-Risk; Gain > No-Gain) and parametric contrasts across reward magnitudes. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described (SPM5; voxelwise t-tests and ANOVAs reported with MNI coordinates and cluster thresholds), and coordinates/clusters are provided in supplementary tables. Participants are healthy human subjects across a wide age range. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a canonical risky decision-making task. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing risky versus riskless decisions (Mean Color > Mean White and Linear Color > Linear White), satisfying the required risky-DM contrast formats. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FSL FLAME, cluster correction) with coordinates/figures/tables and omnibus and pairwise results, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Participant groups (adolescents, including substance users and controls) are acceptable per the eligibility rules. Results are presented in full article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) with supplementary figures/tables; the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that used a risky decision-making task (modified Lane risk-taking task) performed during scanning. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe choices and feedback conditions (risky > safe; win > safe; loss > safe), and both within-condition and condition-by-task interactions (alcohol vs placebo). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and thresholded with cluster correction; results are reported with coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy social drinkers. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing an ambiguous decision-making task (odd/even with certain vs uncertain trials), includes within-task contrasts (Uncertain > Certain), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistics (random-effects 1-sample and between-group t-tests; FWE-corrected maps and coordinate tables). The paper includes methods, results, and discussion describing whole-brain activation and task contrasts, meeting the meta-analysis requirements for ambiguous decision-making studies. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a well-established risky decision-making task. The fMRI analysis includes parametric modulation by pump number (capturing high-risk vs low-risk within trials) and contrasts including active (reward) vs control (white balloon) trials. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-corrected results and coordinates), with mixed-effects between-subject analyses. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods (fMRI acquisition, task, GLM), results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: it used fMRI while participants performed a risky decision-making task (BART) (I4); it reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (Choose Inflate vs. Choose Win; Outcome Inflate vs. Outcome Explode) suitable for risky-DM contrasts (I5); analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level with cluster correction and reported in tables/figures (I6, I8); participant groups (high-risk and healthy youth, ages 10–14) are acceptable (I7). The task is a canonical risky-DM paradigm and contrasts are not against implicit baseline, results are not ROI-only or PET, and whole-text methods, results and figures are present, so no exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study used a perceptual target-detection task with morphed stimuli that manipulated ambiguity and perceptual similarity. It reports within-task condition contrasts (e.g., morph1 vs. target) and uses similarity and ambiguity regressors to predict BOLD, including whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with FDR correction; coordinates and activation maps are reported. Participants are human healthy volunteers. Therefore it meets criteria for an fMRI perceptual decision-making task (I4), provides condition-wise contrasts (I5), reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked results/maps (I6), includes an eligible participant group (I7), and provides whole-brain results/coordinates in text/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports human fMRI during an ambiguous/uncertain decision-making task (matching-pennies). It includes within-task contrasts relevant to ambiguity/uncertainty (e.g., feedback > no-feedback; uncertain > certain; high- vs low-load) and an event-related feedback vs no-feedback contrast. Analyses are group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise maps with reported MNI coordinates/ROIs. Participants are healthy adults. Results are clearly reported in main text (methods, results, discussion). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not only ROI; not contrasts vs baseline only; not connectivity-only; empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study where participants performed the BART (a risky decision-making task). The authors modeled risk level as a parametric modulator of inflation events and computed risk-related contrasts for active and passive modes, then ran whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses (2×2 ANOVA) and reported corrected, voxelwise results. The study therefore provides within-task condition comparisons (active vs passive; risk-level modulation), whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps, and includes human participants (IGD adolescents and healthy controls). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Accordingly, the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy human participants manipulating uncertainty via probabilistic (externally attributed) and knowledge-based (internally attributed) decision tasks. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects) with thresholding and provides coordinates/tables and figures. Relevant contrasts include experimental conditions versus an active control task (control blocks with arrows) and parametric contrasts of increasing uncertainty (high uncertainty > low uncertainty), satisfying the meta-analysis contrast requirements. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans where participants performed a risky decision-making task (skewed gambling) during scanning (I4). The paper reports within-task condition contrasts (skewed vs symmetric; positive vs negative skew) suitable as decision-making contrasts (I5). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are described (voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction, second-level regression analyses), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirement (I6). Participants are healthy adults (I7), and whole-brain results are reported in the text/tables/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>rest), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are provided (not ROI-only), and the task is a risky decision-making paradigm (not excluded task types). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Exclusion rationale: The study employed fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (a decision-making paradigm), but the reported primary contrasts are outcome valence contrasts (reward > punishment) and positive>neutral picture viewing, not contrasts that manipulate or compare levels of risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty as required by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky>safe, high uncertainty>low uncertainty, hard>easy). Therefore it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I5. Exclusion ID met: E5 (task/contrast does not match risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrasts as defined). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI with human participants performing a decision-making task — probabilistic reversal learning), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed), I7 (participant group acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results reported and described). Inclusion ID not met: I5 (required decision-making contrast comparing risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty was not provided). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study tested human participants performing a risky decision-making gambling task (GIG task) during scanning, manipulating risk via risky vs safe options and quota conditions. The fMRI analyses report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts comparing decision conditions (quota-severity contrast and Low/High > Non/Imp and Non/Imp > Low/High), with activation maps and coordinates and cluster correction. Participants were healthy humans. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making, condition-vs-condition contrasts, group whole-brain results, participant eligibility, and availability of results in text/figures. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI, only connectivity without activation, contrasts vs rest only) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study (wheel-of-fortune risky decision task) meets inclusion criteria I4 (task-based fMRI in humans), I5 (risky > safe contrast: 10/30 vs 70/90), and I7 (healthy participant groups). However, the primary neuroimaging analysis was restricted to a priori ROIs with small-volume correction and reported ROI peak coordinates; the paper does not provide an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map required by I6. Because the report presents only ROI-limited results (no whole-brain voxelwise maps), it falls under exclusion E6 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (whole-brain voxelwise group map) and I8 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in tables—no qualifying whole-brain results were provided). Therefore the study must be excluded from the whole-brain meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (biased vs. unbiased decisions on vocal emotions) in healthy human participants. It reports within-task contrasts directly comparing two decision-making conditions (unbiased > biased and biased > unbiased) and presents group-level voxelwise statistical analyses (SPM flexible factorial, thresholded maps) with ROI-masking applied to whole-brain results. The study therefore provides whole-brain, group-level task-evoked activation maps (reported within predefined ROIs) and also reports functional connectivity (PPI) but not exclusively. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not only baseline contrasts, not only connectivity, not only between-group effects). Full text appears complete with Methods, Results, and Discussion. Hence it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This full text reports an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making (categorization) task manipulating motion coherence (perceptual salience) and distance from a category boundary (categorical salience). The paper reports condition-vs-condition analyses including parametric contrasts (e.g., BOLD modulation with motion coherence: low coherence > high coherence) and ANOVA interactions, with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps (cluster-corrected) and ROI confirmation. Participants are healthy adults. The manuscript includes complete sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it satisfies I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (condition/parametric contrasts comparing decision conditions), I6 (whole-brain group voxelwise maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, no task>rest-only contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (framing task) with choices between a sure option and a gamble, satisfying I4. It includes within-task contrasts comparing decision types (e.g., sure vs gamble within gain/loss frames and the framing-effect contrast [(Gsure + Lgamble) − (Lsure + Ggamble)]), satisfying I5. Analyses were conducted at the group level using SPM random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise maps (with thresholding and reported peak coordinates), satisfying I6 and I8. Participants were healthy volunteers (I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion, so is complete. No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>rest), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and task is a risky decision-making task. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI investigation of state-based dynamic reward learning (state-maximizing vs reward-maximizing choices) comparing younger and older adults. However, the task is a history-dependent reward-learning paradigm and does not manipulate or contrast risky vs safe, ambiguous vs non-ambiguous, or perceptual difficulty conditions as defined by the meta-analysis. Exclusion criterion E5 applies (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). The paper does meet some inclusion requirements: it reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps (I6); uses healthy human participants (I7); and presents whole-brain results described in the text/figures (I8). It does not meet I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task) and I5 (it does not report the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Therefore it should be excluded under E5.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human subjects that directly manipulates outcome probability (risk) within a decision-making task (options with differing probabilities and delays) and reports group-level whole-brain task-versus-control contrasts. The authors present a decision-making condition contrasted against active control tasks (summation and visual controls) and report voxelwise random-effects analyses (FWE-corrected results and coordinate tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Although the paradigm also includes delay, the critical manipulation involves probabilistic (risky) choices and a parametric subjective-value regressor; thus it fits the meta-analysis scope of risky decision-making. Full text (methods, results, figures, tables, and coordinates) is available. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, resting-state-only, implicit-baseline-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a decision-making task manipulating outcome uncertainty. The task contrasts two-choice prediction (decision under uncertainty) with an active control (two-choice response task) and explicitly tests an uncertainty contrast (50% error rate vs 20%/80% error rates; contrast vector = high uncertainty > low uncertainty). The analysis is whole-brain, voxelwise (AFNI, Talairach normalization, cluster correction) with group-level mixed-model ANOVA and coordinates/figures reported. Participants include schizophrenia subjects and matched healthy controls. Reporting includes task-versus-control and uncertainty-related contrasts, and whole-brain maps/tables/figures. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a perceptual decision-making task (moving dots) with probabilistic cues. The authors report within-task condition contrasts (reliable vs. neutral and moderate vs. neutral) that probe decision-making processes, and they performed group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with cluster correction and reported coordinates and figures. Participants were healthy adults, and the full manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis criteria for a perceptual decision-making fMRI study and provides whole-brain activation maps suitable for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a Wheel of Fortune task manipulating reward magnitude, probability, and risk. The paper reports within-task contrasts including risky > safe (risk contrast), probability contrasts (low vs high), and magnitude contrasts (high vs low) during the selection phase. Group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise analyses are reported with coordinate tables and corrected cluster thresholds. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of fMRI risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (sequential gambles with targets). The paper reports within-task, parametric contrasts (regressors for target level, expected value, variance/risk, skewness) and tests neural correlates of these decision variables at the group level using SPM; results are reported as voxelwise group analyses with stereotactic coordinates and thresholds (whole-brain results and small-volume corrections). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making (I4), contains within-task contrasts/parametric comparisons relevant to risky decisions (I5), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I6), uses an eligible participant sample (I7), and provides whole-brain results in text/tables/figures (I8). The provided full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an original fMRI study in humans that measured brain activation while participants performed a risky decision-making task (repeated choices between a risky stock and a safe bond). It reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., stock vs. bond choice in the gain domain — equivalent to risky > safe) and conducts group-level, whole-brain analyses (SPM group-level contrasts, whole-brain FWE-corrected results reported). Participants are healthy adult males. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (experimental design, fMRI acquisition and preprocessing, GLMs), Results (whole-brain and ROI results), and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not only baseline contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete for screening purposes. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky decision-making and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing an explicit risky decision-making gambling task with explicit probabilities and reward/punishment conditions. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise analyses and contrasts of task conditions against a neutral control (reward>neutral, loss>neutral), satisfying the required task-versus-control contrast form. Whole-brain results are reported (tables/coordinates) and ROI analyses are supplementary. Full article contains complete Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study used fMRI while participants performed a two-choice prediction task manipulating error rates (20%, 50%, 80%), which operationalizes risky and ambiguous decision-making. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables of significant clusters/coordinates and corrected thresholds. Analyses included comparisons across error-rate conditions and interoception states (e.g., effects during 80% punishment vs other conditions and Group x ER x Interoception interactions), providing within-task condition-vs-condition contrasts rather than only task>implicit-baseline contrasts. Participant groups include methamphetamine users and healthy controls, which is acceptable. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply based on the full text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in healthy humans that used a probabilistic choice task (participants chose higher vs lower than 5 for cues with 85% vs 65% predictive probabilities). The task involves decision-making under differing levels of uncertainty (easy = low uncertainty; hard = high uncertainty), and the paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM statistical maps and coordinates (random-effects SPMs) with contrasts that include cue difficulty (easy > hard / high uncertainty > low uncertainty) and learning-type contrasts. Thus the study provides within-task condition-versus-condition contrasts mapping onto ambiguous decision-making (high uncertainty > low uncertainty), meets whole-brain reporting, and includes appropriate participant sampling. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during decision-making under uncertainty), I5 (condition contrast: hard vs easy/high uncertainty vs low uncertainty), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (eligible participant group), I8 (results reported with coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a decision-making task manipulating uncertainty (certain vs uncertain trials). The authors report a within-task contrast (uncertain > certain) that maps ambiguity-related activation and conduct group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects, whole-brain thresholds) with results described in text, tables, and figures. Participants include clinical (alcoholic) and healthy groups, both acceptable. The task and contrasts directly match ambiguous decision-making criteria (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, not only connectivity, and not non-empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, so fulltext is complete.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using the Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART), a well-established risky decision-making task, with analyses linking neural activation to increasing risk (balloon size/adjusted pumps). It provides a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical map (correlation maps transformed to z-scores and t-tested at group level) and reports peak coordinates and corrected thresholds. The neural contrast is a within-task parametric modulation of risk level (effectively high-risk > low-risk), satisfying the required decision-making contrast forms. Participants include adolescents with TBI and healthy controls (eligible sample types). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest-only, and within-task whole-brain effects are reported). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in which adolescents performed a lottery choice (risk) decision-making task during BOLD acquisition. The authors modeled a parametric regressor of coefficient of variation (CV) of chosen gambles and report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (cluster-level FWE-corrected), showing greater right amygdala activation to higher-risk versus lower-risk choices (equivalent to a 'high-risk > low-risk' contrast). The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. The task and reported contrasts meet the risky-DM specifications, whole-brain maps/coordinates are provided, and none of the exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity- or baseline-only). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study uses an intertemporal choice (delay discounting) task (temporal discounting / Intertemporal Choice Task). The meta-analysis explicitly excludes delay discounting/intertemporal choice tasks (Exclusion E5). The paper does include group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and condition-vs-control contrasts (satisfying I6 and I8), and participant groups are acceptable (I7). However it does not examine risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (I4 not met) and therefore does not provide the eligible risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts required (I5 not met). Full text appears complete. Accordingly the study must be excluded under E5.

This study is excluded because its task is social decision-making (emotion recognition of morphed faces), which falls under exclusion criterion E5 (social decision-making is a non-qualifying task per E5). Despite exclusion, the paper does meet several inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI was conducted while participants performed an ambiguous decision-making task involving uncertain/ambiguous facial expressions), I5 (it reports within-task contrasts comparing decision events: last face > previous faces), I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported, with FWE-corrected results), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: []. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded solely because it violates E5 (task domain: social decision-making), even though it otherwise provides appropriate fMRI whole-brain contrasts and analyses.

This study used fMRI while participants performed a spatial memory retrieval task in morphing virtual environments, not a canonical risky, ambiguous economic, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Although participants made memory-based placement choices in ambiguous contexts, the paper’s analyses focus on MVPA pattern similarity (sigmoidal vs linear models) and hippocampal remapping rather than standard decision-making contrasts (e.g., ambiguous > non-ambiguous) or univariate whole-brain task-evoked activation maps appropriate for the meta-analysis. Exclusion ID E5 applies (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as defined by the review). Inclusion IDs met: I4 (fMRI during task), I7 (acceptable participant groups), and I8 (reporting of coordinates/whole-brain results in text/figures). Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no standard contrast comparing decision conditions or task > control as required), I6 (no clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps presented for the decision contrasts). Full text appears complete.

This study used fMRI while participants performed a perceptual phoneme categorization task (auditory post-tests) and reports group-level whole-brain random-effects maps (satisfies I4, I6, I8). However, it does not report a qualifying decision-making contrast as required by I5 (e.g., hard>easy, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or a task>active control). The primary whole-brain contrasts presented are audiovisual exposure blocks > baseline and a behaviorally weighted parametric modulation of exposure-block activation predicting later perception; no explicit within-scan contrasts directly comparing decision-making conditions (e.g., ambiguous vs less-ambiguous post-tests or hard vs easy perceptual trials) are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5. Exclusion criterion E3 applies because the study’s main whole-brain task contrast is versus baseline and no appropriate condition-vs-condition decision-making contrast is provided. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human fMRI study using a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) with participants scanned during decisions. The paper reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (Risk vs. No-Risk; Risk > No-Risk and No-Risk > Risk) that match admissible risky-DM contrasts (risk > certainty). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (FLAME) are reported with cluster-corrected results and tables/figures. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion, enabling extraction of whole-brain activation coordinates and contrasts of interest for the meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a risky decision-making paradigm (Risky Gains Task) in human participants and includes within-task contrasts (risky vs safe decisions; risky wins vs losses). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results (AFNI preprocessing, voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction via updated 3dFWHMx/3dClustSim) with tables/figures reporting significant clusters and coordinates. Participant sample (occasional stimulant users) is acceptable per the review’s participant inclusivity. The paper provides full Methods, Results and Discussion sections and clearly describes the relevant contrasts, satisfying inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met: contrasts are condition-vs-condition not task>rest, modality is fMRI not PET, the task is a risky-DM task (not excluded task types), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and the study reports task activation maps rather than only connectivity or resting-state findings. Thus the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This article reports an fMRI study in human participants performing a monetary guessing task with uncertain outcomes (decision-making under uncertainty), satisfying the risky decision-making domain. The study includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports task contrasts (gain > loss; feedback and reward-relevant trials versus reward-neutral control trials are modeled), with cluster-corrected whole-brain results presented in figures and tables. Participants are human (healthy young adults). Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision task), I5 (within-task contrast comparing decision-making conditions and task vs control), I6 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables) are met. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI analyses, PET, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).
