This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants using a decision-making task that involves uncertainty about outcomes and feedback during learning. It includes within-task contrasts comparing high-uncertainty (exploratory) versus low-uncertainty (proficiency) phases and contrasts of gains vs. losses and correct vs. wrong feedback, i.e. condition-versus-condition comparisons relevant to ambiguous/risky decision-making. Group-level, whole-brain (SPM2) voxelwise analyses are reported with coordinates and cluster results. Participants are healthy adult females. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables, coordinates) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET only, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous decision-making.

This is an fMRI study in humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (face vs. house categorization) with manipulated asymmetric costs. It includes within-task contrasts comparing decision-making conditions (e.g., (FV+HV)>2NV, FV>HV, HV>FV) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster- and SVC-corrected results) with coordinates and statistical inference. Participants are healthy human volunteers. Whole-brain results are described in the text and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not resting-state-only, not non-empirical, and includes condition-vs-condition contrasts rather than task>rest). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making that reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (high-risk vs low-risk; high-risk vs equal-risk; risk/reward vs control) in an adolescent sample, so it meets I4 (fMRI), I5 (decision-making contrasts), and I7 (eligible participant groups). However, the paper only reports ROI-constrained voxelwise tests (small-volume correction within pre-specified prefrontal ROIs) and presents ROI-based activations/coordinates rather than an unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Although the authors state that activations were collected brain-wide, all reported statistical tests and inference are restricted to a priori ROIs (SVC), and no whole-brain, unmasked group statistical maps or whole-brain voxelwise results are provided. This violates inclusion criterion I6 and falls under exclusion criterion E6 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study with healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (categorizing average color/shape). The authors report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise SPM8 analyses (parametric and contrast-based tests of mean-related and variance-related uncertainty) with peak coordinates and cluster-corrected results, satisfying contrasts equivalent to hard>easy / uncertainty contrasts. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not rest-baseline-only contrasts, and task is perceptual DM).

This is a prospective fMRI study in human adolescents using a risky decision-making paradigm (Wheel of Fortune) with explicit probabilities. It reports within-task contrasts comparing high vs moderate and high/moderate vs equal risk/reward conditions and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses corrected for multiple comparisons, with results described in text, figures, and tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, scan acquisition, preprocessing, group analyses), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study where participants performed the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART) during task-based fMRI, providing within-task contrasts based on risk level (parametric 'risk level' pump regressor) and reporting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (cluster- and voxel-level thresholds). The manuscript includes methods, results, and discussion (full text present) and reports whole-brain results in the text (with supplemental materials referenced). Although the paper also presents resting-state connectivity analyses, it also provides task-evoked whole-brain contrasts appropriate for risky decision-making (high-risk > low-risk type parametric contrast). Participant sample (nicotine-dependent smokers) is an allowed population. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest only, or only connectivity without task maps) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for risky decision-making task fMRI and whole-brain reporting.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that directly probes risky decision-making using monetary gambles (high-probability small payoff vs low-probability large payoff). The paper reports within-task and between-task contrasts (parametric regressors for intradimensional vs unidimensional differences; preferential choice vs judgment-based choice paired t-tests), and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM5; cluster-corrected results, reported peak MNI coordinates). Results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps/coordinates and figures. Subjects are healthy adults. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky decision task), I5 (condition-vs-condition and task-vs-task contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/figures). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

The study used fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (I4), reported group-level whole-brain task-evoked results with cluster-level FWE correction (I6), included an eligible participant sample (I7), and presented whole-brain results in text/tables/figures (I8). However, it does not report any of the required decision-making contrasts specified by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy). Instead, the fMRI analysis used model-derived parametric modulators for reward prediction errors (RPEcue and RPEoutcome) and between-group comparisons of those parametric effects; no within-task contrast of risky vs safe or ambiguous vs non-ambiguous (I5) is provided. Because I5 is not met, the study does not satisfy all inclusion criteria and must be excluded. Exclusion criteria met: none of the explicit exclusion items (e.g., PET only, ROI-only) apply. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I5.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults that directly examines ambiguous decision-making (internal vs external subjective color choices) with within-task contrasts (ISD vs ESD, ISD vs EVD, ESD vs EVD). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported (SPM2, FDR-corrected voxelwise results, tables/figures), and contrasts are against an active veridical control (EVD) rather than rest. The paradigm therefore meets criteria for ambiguous decision-making, provides task-versus-task and ambiguous-versus-control contrasts, and reports whole-brain voxelwise group results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; not PET, not ROI-only, and not resting-state/connectivity-only.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choices between sure amounts and gambles with varying probabilities/magnitudes). It includes within-task contrasts addressing risk levels (high-risk vs low-risk loss conditions) and feedback effects, and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with familywise-error correction (i.e., whole-brain statistical maps). Participant groups (binge drinkers and healthy volunteers) are acceptable. Whole-brain results are described in text and figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET; not ROI-only; contains within-task condition contrasts rather than only task>baseline; reports whole-brain activation maps). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and is INCLUDED.

This is an empirical human fMRI study in which participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (orientation discrimination of Gabor patches with manipulated discriminability/contrast). The analysis included within-task comparisons that index perceptual difficulty/discriminability (high- vs low-contrast trials, implemented via trial-by-trial parametric regressors and model comparisons), and reported group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (SPM2 random-effects ANOVA with voxelwise thresholds and coordinates). Participants were healthy adults. The paper therefore meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI perceptual decision-making contrasts and whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (BART) during scanning, with appropriate within-task contrasts and task-vs-control contrasts (PumpsParametric > ControlParametric, PumpsAvg > ControlAvg). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported with cluster correction and peak coordinates; both within-group and between-group effects are presented. Participants (young smokers and nonsmokers) are within allowable groups. The provided full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>baseline-only contrasts) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescents that used a risky decision-making task (the Social Analogue Risk Task) during scanning and reports whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps. The authors modeled knock, cash-out, and slam events and used a parametric modulator (cash-out PM) indexing increasing risk (number of knocks) and conducted whole-brain group analyses (including cluster-corrected results). Results (main effects and regressions) are reported across the whole brain in the text and figures. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (within-task contrast via parametric modulation of risk/cash-out), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (human adolescent sample acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a risky decision-making (mixed-gamble) task (I4). The paper includes condition-vs-condition contrasts and tests of decision factors (e.g., positive vs negative EV, high vs low uncertainty, high vs low urgency, and interactions)—satisfying the required decision-making contrasts (I5). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise (SPM8 flexible factorial second-level analysis; voxelwise thresholding and cluster correction), and whole-brain results are reported (I6, I8). Participants are healthy humans (I7), which is an eligible group. No exclusion criteria are met: the study does not rely solely on task>rest contrasts (it reports direct condition contrasts), is not PET, includes whole-brain results (not ROI-only), and is an empirical fMRI activation study. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults that used a risky decision-making task (Modified Cups Task) during scanning and reports within-task contrasts comparing decisions after losses vs after wins (riskloss > riskwin and vice versa). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with cluster-corrected thresholds and MNI coordinates. The task and contrasts directly probe risky decision-making and meet the meta-analysis focus. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and contrasts are condition-versus-condition rather than baseline). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the report appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human adults performing the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky decision-making task). The authors report a within-task contrast 'risky decisions minus safe decisions' (risky > safe), performed at the group-level using random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (statistical parametric maps, voxel- and cluster-level thresholds) and report coordinates/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus the study meets fMRI task (I4), appropriate decision-making contrast (I5), whole-brain group-level analysis (I6), participant eligibility (I7), and reporting of coordinates/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a well-established risky decision-making paradigm (experimental gamble vs control gamble) with contrasts of interest (experimental>control; high vs low probability; high vs low gain) and separate decision and outcome phases. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FLAME for within-group effects and OLS for between-group effects) with cluster-corrected thresholds and reported peak coordinates/tables. Participants include substance-using and control groups. Thus the study provides whole-brain, group-level task activation maps for risky decision-making and meets the meta-analysis requirements for risky-DM contrasts and whole-brain reporting. Full text appears complete (methods, results, tables, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (direction-of-motion discrimination) with two coherence levels. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and condition-versus-condition contrasts (high-coherence vs low-coherence; conjunction analyses across response modalities), and provides coordinates and statistical maps. The methods and results include mixed-effects whole-brain GLM analyses and thresholded Z-statistic images, satisfying the review’s requirements for task-evoked whole-brain results. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study in which human participants performed a categorization task that includes ambiguous decision trials (inverse base rate effect). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., comparisons of activation on ambiguous trials depending on response type and model-based parametric modulators for similarity vs. dissimilarity evidence) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (cluster-corrected) with tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults and full methods, results, and discussion are present. No exclusion criteria are met (no PET, no ROI-only, not task>rest only). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria for ambiguous decision-making fMRI (I4), contains relevant within-task contrasts (I5), reports group whole-brain maps (I6), involves an eligible participant group (I7), and reports whole-brain results in text/figures/tables consistent with acceptable reporting (I8).

This is an fMRI study in human participants that used a perceptual two-alternative forced-choice task (judge stimulus as more speech vs more non-speech). The experiment manipulated stimulus ambiguity/difficulty (pure vs blended stimuli) and modeledcondition-wise BOLD responses (Speech: speech vs non-speech; Correctness; Time), and conducted group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and reported peak coordinates. Thus it provides within-task, condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making and reports whole-brain group activation maps/coordinates. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (choices between sure wins and lotteries) while scanned. The paper reports within-task contrasts (presence vs absence of advice; parametric modulators for offer magnitude and certainty equivalents indexing safe vs risky valuation) and whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses (cluster-level corrected t-maps, reported coordinates and brain maps). Participants include adolescents and adults (healthy), and results are presented in main text and supplementary materials. Thus it meets all inclusion requirements for fMRI risky decision-making contrasts and whole-brain reporting. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study used simultaneous EEG-fMRI with human participants performing a probabilistic reversal-learning task (meets I4). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise fMRI results (meets I6) with acceptable participant sample (meets I7) and whole-brain results presented in text/tables (meets I8). However, it does not present at least one contrast that matches the meta-analysis’ required decision-making contrasts (I5) — e.g., there is no reported ‘risky > safe’, ‘high-risk > low-risk’, ‘high uncertainty > low uncertainty’, or perceptual ‘hard > easy’ contrast during the decision phase. The reported contrasts/regressors are outcome-locked parametric regressors for prediction-error valence and surprise (EEG-informed and model-based), not the decision-condition contrasts required by inclusion criterion I5. Therefore the study fails to satisfy all inclusion criteria and must be excluded.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study in human adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Colorado Balloon Game) with explicit contrasts between risky decision trials (DecBa) and an active control/baseline directed trial (DirBa) for decision, win, and loss periods. The analyses are whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise maps (SPM) reported with cluster- and voxel-level corrections and coordinates. Participants include clinical (ASD) and control groups (adolescents), which are acceptable. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not rest-baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a risky decision-making task (Stoplight driving simulation) with human adolescents. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing risky versus safe decisions (Go > Stop and Stop > Go) and feedback contrasts (Crash vs No-Crash). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (voxelwise threshold p = .001, cluster thresholds; tables of coordinates and figures provided). The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making whole-brain activation contrasts.

This study meets the review inclusion criteria: it used fMRI while participants performed a probabilistic reversal-learning task that manipulates outcome uncertainty (risk/ambiguity). The primary imaging contrasts compare punished (probabilistic error) versus rewarded correct responses (a within-task condition-versus-condition contrast relevant to decision-making under uncertainty). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise (SPM, cluster-level FWE correction) with results reported in tables/figures and described in the text. Participant groups (ADHD persisters/remitters and matched controls) are acceptable per eligibility. No exclusion criteria are met: the paper does not report only ROI-only analyses, only connectivity, only PET, or only task>baseline contrasts — it reports whole-brain task activation and within-group contrasts. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Accordingly, include the study.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy human subjects performing a perceptual decision-making (animal detection) task with manipulated motivation. Relevant contrasts meeting the review definitions are reported (NEGATIVE > NEUTRAL, POSITIVE > NEUTRAL; task blocks also contrasted against an active arrow baseline). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are performed and reported (FWE-corrected whole-brain tables and figures), and ROI results are supplementary — i.e., whole-brain results are available. The task is a perceptual decision-making paradigm (detection), so it fits the perceptual-DM category. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not PET, not rest-only contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and is empirical fMRI). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Full text reports an fMRI study in human participants performing a decision-making card prediction task manipulating outcome uncertainty (uncertain vs. certain). The paper includes an explicit Uncertain > Certain (Uncertain–Certain action selection) contrast, computed voxelwise and tested at the group level with whole-brain analyses and cluster correction; significant clusters and coordinates are reported in Table 2. Participant groups (stimulant users and controls) are acceptable per review scope. The manuscript contains complete core sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for an fMRI study of ambiguous/risky decision-making with a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrast and reported coordinates.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy humans investigating decision-making under outcome uncertainty with a probabilistic (60%/40%) two-alternative sampling task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses and contrasts of task conditions versus an active control (information-gathering > counting; decision event > counting), with coordinates and thresholding described. Thus it meets the review’s scope (risky/probabilistic decision-making) and satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI task, task>control contrasts, whole-brain group analysis, participant eligibility, and reporting of whole-brain results. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and no exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task>rest only, non-empirical) are met.

This longitudinal fMRI study used the Wheel of Fortune risky decision-making task and reports a risky vs. safe selection contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (AFNI 3dANOVA3) with cluster correction and results reported in tables/figures (Table 2, Figures). Participants include adolescents who became binge drinkers and matched controls (acceptable participant groups). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no baseline-only contrasts, not PET, task is risky-DM, reports whole-brain results beyond ROIs, not only connectivity, includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete.

This study reports an fMRI investigation of decision-making under uncertainty using a modified “beads” task (ambiguous decision-making). It includes an explicit task-versus-active-control contrast (DECISION > COUNTING), performed as whole-brain, group-level analyses (SPM5) with coordinates and figures reported. Participant groups (schizophrenia patients and healthy controls) are acceptable. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and thus appears complete. All required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no implicit-baseline-only contrasts, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical).

Although this fMRI study used a probabilistic (65% vs 35%) reward-learning task (meets I4) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (meets I6) with results described in the text/tables (meets I8) and an eligible participant sample (meets I7), it does not include any of the required decision-making contrasts specified by the review (e.g., “risky > safe”, “high-risk > low-risk”, “risk > certainty”, or an explicit decision-task > control-task contrast). The reported analyses focus on parametric RPE and value regressors and emotional (fearful vs neutral) modulations, not on between-condition decision-making contrasts of risk/ambiguity or hard>easy perceptual difficulty. Therefore Inclusion Criterion I5 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from E3–E9 are directly met, but failure to meet I5 mandates exclusion.

This is an fMRI study in healthy humans that directly examines perceptual decision-making (emotion vs. gender categorizations of faces). It reports condition-vs-control contrasts (emotion > control, gender > control) and direct decision-condition contrasts (emotion > gender and vice versa), meeting the required perceptual-DM contrast forms. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain mixed-effects voxelwise maps with corrected cluster thresholds and reported activation coordinates/tables/figures. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, and contrasts are against an active control task rather than implicit baseline).

The study is excluded because it does not meet the requirement that participants performed a decision-making task (Exclusion E5). Although the task manipulates uncertainty (reward vs. no-incentive anticipation) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps, it is a passive slot-machine paradigm with no behavioral choices or decision-making component; thus inclusion criteria I4 (decision-making task) and I5 (at least one decision-making contrast/comparison) are not satisfied. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results reported), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (contrast comparing decision-making conditions or task vs active control for decision-making). Full text is complete and sufficient for this determination.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a probabilistic wheel-of-fortune task (risky decision-making). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and contrasts of decision task versus non-reward control trials (e.g., anticipation [AR1, AR2, AR3] > AnRn; outcome contrasts versus OnwRn), satisfying the requirement for condition-versus-control contrasts. The full text includes methods, results, and tables of coordinates and description of whole-brain findings, meeting whole-brain evidence reporting. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is a whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing a risky decision-making task (mixed gambles) with within-subject condition contrasts. The paper reports condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., Play > Pass, Gain > Loss, and their interaction), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with cluster- and FWE-correction, and provides coordinates in tables/figures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although the study used fMRI in humans performing a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task (I4), reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (I6), included healthy participants (I7), and presented whole-brain results in text/figures (I8), it does not report a decision-making contrast that matches the meta-analysis inclusion forms (e.g., risky>safe, high-risk>low-risk, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, hard>easy). The primary reported contrasts are reward vs neutral, loss vs neutral, and parametric prediction-error regressors rather than the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision contrasts (I5 not met). No exclusion criteria from E3–E9 are triggered. Therefore excluded for failing to meet I5.

This is an fMRI study using a mixed gambles task (50/50 gains/losses) that probes risky decision-making in human participants (adolescents and adults). The study reports within-task condition contrasts (e.g., Accepted Trials > Rejected Trials and Rejected Trials > Accepted Trials) as well as Accepted/Rejected trials versus baseline, and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-corrected maps and coordinate tables. Participants are healthy human subjects across relevant ages. Therefore the paper meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no PET, no ROI-only, not only baseline contrasts, and includes within-task condition contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (I6) and tests uncertainty-related contrasts (e.g., variance/inverted-U; consistent with “high uncertainty > low uncertainty”) and thus meets I5, and the participant sample is acceptable (I7) and results are clearly reported (I8), the scanned task was a passive conditioning/imperative task (participants pressed a button indicating stimulus quadrant) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task performed during fMRI. The authors explicitly state they used conditioning “to study the processing of economic parameters independent of choice.” Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I4 (task must be a decision-making task performed during fMRI). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criterion not met: I4. Exclusion criteria met: none ([]).

This is an fMRI study in human healthy adults that explicitly manipulates and reports neural correlates of decision-making under uncertainty (relative and mean uncertainty). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise statistical maps (coordinates, FWE-corrected clusters) linking trial-by-trial relative uncertainty to BOLD in RLPFC and mean uncertainty to DLPFC/SPL. Analyses include parametric contrasts (high vs low uncertainty effects) and group contrasts (explorers vs nonexplorers), satisfying the requirement for a decision-making contrast beyond implicit baseline. Methods, results, and coordinates are reported in the main text (with supplemental materials available), and the task involves ambiguous/uncertain decision-making (uncertainty-driven exploration), which fits the meta-analysis’ ambiguous-DM domain. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, resting-state-only, non-eligible task) are met.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing an ambiguous decision-making task (the HiLo game). It includes condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., 50% uncertainty vs 100% certainty; linear contrasts across uncertainty levels) that directly test ambiguity-related decision processes. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted using FLAME with cluster correction (z>2.3, p<.05), and coordinates for significant clusters (ACC: x=-2,y=22,z=38) are reported. Participants are healthy adolescents and adults within the eligible age range. Thus the study meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI ambiguous decision-making, condition contrasts, and whole-brain results. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the perceptual decision-making meta-analysis. It used fMRI while human participants performed multiple perceptual decision-making tasks (face–house, happy–angry face, audiovisual synchrony/asynchrony, and random-dot-motion), satisfying I4. The paper reports condition-vs-condition contrasts that map directly onto perceptual-DM comparisons (e.g., difficult > easy; low coherence > high coherence; asynchrony vs synchrony; noisy > clear), satisfying I5. Analyses were performed at the group level using SPM with whole-brain, random-effects second-level maps and corrected thresholds; activations are reported in tables/figures, satisfying I6 and I8. Participants are healthy adults (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not task>rest) so E3 is not met; imaging modality is fMRI (E4 not met); tasks are perceptual DM (E5 not met); whole-brain results are provided (E6 not met); the paper also reports activations beyond connectivity analyses (E7 not met); this is empirical fMRI data (E9 not met). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, tables). Therefore include.

This study acquired fMRI while participants performed a probabilistic reversal-learning task (decision-making under uncertainty), and reports within-task contrasts (loseshift > winstay; final error > error) that compare decision-making conditions. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise with multiple-comparison correction and reported coordinates/figures/tables. Participant groups (schizophrenia and controls) are acceptable. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext appears complete). Contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>rest), it is not PET, and it provides whole-brain results rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a two-alternative perceptual decision-making task (face vs house) with manipulated stimulus coherence. It reports within-task contrasts comparing difficulty levels (hard > easy) and DR>RT, uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses (FLAME) with cluster correction and reports MNI coordinates and cluster statistics. Behavioral modeling and DDM-informed analyses are included. The study therefore satisfies perceptual-decision criteria, provides condition-vs-condition contrasts (hard>easy), and supplies whole-brain group-level results (maps/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not only baseline contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study is EXCLUDED because it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as required (Exclusion E5). The tasks are value-based/affective decisions about pleasantness of thermal and olfactory stimuli (reward-based choice) rather than risky/uncertain or perceptual-coherence decisions targeted by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (within-task condition contrast: easy vs difficult), I6 (group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (task category — not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). The full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports fMRI data collected while human participants performed the Iowa Gambling Task (a risky/ambiguous decision-making task). It includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (disadvantageous decks vs advantageous decks — corresponding to risky > safe) as well as decision > baseline contrasts, and presents group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) within-group and between-group statistical maps (whole-brain corrected thresholds reported). Participant samples are acceptable per inclusion criteria. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI risky/ambiguous decision-making with whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (the study does not rely solely on implicit baseline contrasts, is not PET, includes whole-brain maps beyond ROI or connectivity-only results, and reports within-group task effects).

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans performing a probabilistic two-armed bandit decision-making task (uncertain/risky reward learning). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FWE-corrected maps) for a decision-related parametric contrast (chosen expected value Q at time of choice) and for outcome-related RPE regressors, satisfying the requirement for a within-task, decision-related contrast. Participants are healthy human adults (younger and older). Whole-brain results are presented with coordinates and figures. Although the study also collected PET, it is not a PET-only paper and includes unmasked, whole-brain fMRI activation maps. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This article reports an fMRI study in which healthy human participants performed a risky decision-making task (the BART) during scanning, includes within-task contrasts (parametric risk modulation; experimental green (risk) > control orange balloon; decision contrasts cash > inflate), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE correction and coordinate tables. The sample and methods are fully described in the full text. Thus all inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

Although the study acquired whole‑brain group fMRI data during a task involving risk (detection probability) and reports Dis vs Hon contrasts at the outcome phase, it is a social/moral dishonesty paradigm rather than a canonical risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision‑making task. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the task is social/moral decision‑making (dishonesty) which the metaanalysis excludes. Moreover, the reported fMRI contrasts focus on outcome presentation (Dis vs Hon at feedback) rather than decision‑period contrasts of interest (e.g., risky > safe); therefore inclusion criterion I5 (at least one decision‑making contrast) is not met in this paper. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (fMRI during a risky/uncertain task), I6 (group-level whole‑brain voxelwise maps), I7 (eligible participant group), I8 (whole‑brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no decision‑period risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast reported). Full text appears complete. Given E5 is met, the study must be excluded from the decision‑making meta‑analysis.

This fMRI study tested risky decision-making (child-friendly cake gambling task) during scanning with healthy human participants, reporting contrasts comparing decision conditions (high-risk > low-risk; negative > positive feedback). It includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (exploratory whole-brain section, tables of activations and figures) and reports coordinates and ROI results. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and is complete. All inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no contrasts only versus baseline, no PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This study reports task-based fMRI in humans during a risky decision-making task (Colorado Balloon Game) with explicit risky vs. cautious choices and decision-periods (I4). It uses an active control condition (Directed Trials) and reports the key contrast (Decision Trial – Directed Trial) and separate analyses for risky vs. cautious deliberation, satisfying the allowed decision>control and within-task contrasts (I5). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level random-effects SPM8 maps with cluster-level FWE correction and reported cluster/tables/figures, meeting whole-brain evidence and reporting requirements (I6, I8). Participant groups include adolescents with conduct/substance problems and matched comparisons, which are acceptable per eligibility (I7). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusions.

This is an empirical fMRI study in adolescents performing a risky decision-making task (Risky-Gains). It reports within-group and between-group, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses including a risky > safe contrast (risky vs safe choices) and reward vs punishment contrasts. Results are reported as whole-brain analyses with tables/figures and coordinates. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (risky fMRI task; appropriate contrasts; whole-brain group-level maps; acceptable participant group; coordinates/figures reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a limited-offer decision task that manipulates risk/uncertainty (accept vs wait with chance of losing the offer). The authors report group-level, voxelwise SPM analyses (whole-brain and ROI), including parametric contrasts for choice conflict (entropy/high vs low) and expected precision (state-dependent confidence), with reported whole-brain significant clusters and midbrain ROI peaks. These constitute within-task condition comparisons (e.g., high vs low conflict/precision) relevant to risky/uncertain decision-making. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision-making), I5 (within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions via parametric modulators), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (human participant sample acceptable), and I8 (results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not only baseline contrasts; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; empirical data). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making (Cups task) with an explicit risky>safe contrast (I4, I5). Participants are humans and age range fits (I7), and results/coordinates are reported in detail (I8). However, the paper's reported group-level task activation results for the risky>safe contrast were analyzed/thresholded within an a priori anterior insula ROI rather than presented as a whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map. While the study does report whole-brain PPI (connectivity) results, it does not provide a whole-brain group-level task activation map for the decision contrast, so it effectively reports ROI-only task activation (violates inclusion I6) and thus meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only, no whole-brain task results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face vs house) with manipulated sensory evidence (high vs low coherence). The authors report within-task contrasts directly relevant to perceptual DM (High>Low and Low>High sensory evidence; sensory task vs baseline) and additional contrasts for motor preparation (eye/hand). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain (mixed-effects FLAME1+2) voxelwise statistical maps with cluster correction; results are reported in text, figures, and tables. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and none of the exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study reports an empirical fMRI investigation in 9–11 year-old humans performing a risky decision-making task (Colorado Balloon Game). It includes within-task contrasts comparing Decision versus Directed (control) trials (e.g., risky Decision > Directed sham trials), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM with nonparametric permutation testing) with tables and figures of significant clusters. Participant characteristics fall within eligible age groups. Results are reported in the main text and tables (whole-brain coordinates/clusters), satisfying the meta-analysis’ reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete for screening.

This is a human fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (images of pianos/chairs) that manipulated stimulus discriminability (high/medium/low) and analysed task difficulty (decreasing stimulus quality = hard > easy) and trial-by-trial RT effects. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) GLMs were reported with FWE-corrected results and clusters in tables/figures. Contrasts correspond to perceptual-DM comparisons (e.g., low > high stimulus quality / hard > easy), satisfying the review’s contrast requirements. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study that directly contrasts decision-making conditions based on uncertainty (Uncertainty > Certainty) during a multiple-choice task. The contrast corresponds to ambiguous/uncertainty decision-making (e.g., “high uncertainty > low uncertainty”). The study reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8), with MNI coordinates and corrected/unadjusted thresholds, and provides multiple within-task condition-versus-condition contrasts (Uncertainty>Certainty, LC>OE, etc.). Participants were healthy human subjects. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI ambiguous/risky/perceptual decision-making studies and does not violate any exclusion criteria (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, empirical, whole-brain results provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of risky economic decision-making (mixed lotteries) conducted in human participants (MDD and healthy controls), satisfying I4. The analysis includes condition-wise parametric modulators for gains and losses and directly contrasts gain versus loss coding (gains > losses and losses > gains) and group interactions, satisfying I5. The paper reports group-level voxelwise analyses with whole-brain results and coordinates (including whole-brain and ROI-corrected findings, supplementary tables/figures) meeting I6 and I8. Participant groups (MDD and HC) are acceptable per I7. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not PET (E4), does not use only baseline contrasts (it uses condition contrasts, so E3 not met), reports whole-brain results (not ROI-only, E6), is not connectivity/resting-only (E7), includes within-group task effects (E8), and is empirical (not E9). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults performing risky decision-making tasks (lotteries) and social strategic games involving uncertainty. The paper reports within-task condition contrasts (e.g., risky/B-choice vs sure/A-choice; entry games > lotteries/stag-hunt; non-threshold vs threshold) and group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses with reported MNI coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Results are presented in text, figures, and coordinates. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8. No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain analyses are reported; contrasts are condition-versus-condition, not task>rest; modality is fMRI). Full text appears complete.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in humans performing a decision-making task (four-armed bandit) with probabilistic rewards (risk), and thus addresses risky decision-making. It includes task-based, within-task contrasts via model-based parametric regressors (baseline prediction error and novelty-bonus-related prediction error) and contrasts comparing choices of novel versus familiar options, which qualify as decision-making condition contrasts. Analyses were performed at the group level using voxelwise, whole-brain SPM5 random-effects analyses (with results reported and small-volume correction for a priori regions), and participants were healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of valuation/anticipation of rewards and punishments where participants provided pleasantness ratings for cues predicting outcomes. The task does not involve risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (no choices under risk/uncertainty or perceptual difficulty), and no contrasts of the form required by the review (e.g., risky > safe, ambiguous > non-ambiguous, hard > easy) are reported. Therefore it does not meet the core inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Explicitly: Exclusion ID met: E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making). Inclusion IDs met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task maps reported), I7 (acceptable participant group — healthy humans), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (at least one decision-making contrast of the admitted forms). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study used event-related fMRI with group-level whole-brain analyses in healthy humans and reports coordinate-based results (I4, I6, I7, I8 satisfied). However, the task is a probabilistic reversal-learning paradigm examining reversal learning and responses to negative feedback, not an explicit risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making manipulation as defined by the review (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy). The reported contrasts (final reversal errors vs correct responses, probabilistic errors vs correct, etc.) do not match the required decision-making contrasts (I5 not met). Therefore the study does not address the meta-analysis objective and must be excluded (E5). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (two-option lottery Selection task) with fMRI acquisition and group-level whole-brain analyses. Reported task contrasts include within-task decision contrasts such as riskier > surer, gains > losses, and choice-determined value contrasts, satisfying the required risky-DM contrasts. Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise, with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates reported in tables/supplementary materials. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, rest-baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria and is suitable for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in humans performing a risky decision-making card gambling task (meets I4). It reports explicit condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to risky DM (risk scaled linear contrast; high-risk wins > low-risk wins) matching accepted risky-DM contrast forms (meets I5). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level maps with reported cluster coordinates and corrected p-values (meets I6). Participants are healthy humans (meets I7). Whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures and clearly described (meets I8). No exclusion criteria are violated: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not only task>rest), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results provided, not ROI/ connectivity-only, and the paper is empirical. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports an fMRI study in human participants performing the Paper-Scissors-Rock (PSR) decision-making task, which uses predetermined probabilities for preferred/even/worst responses (90%, 50%, 10%), constituting risky/uncertain decision-making. The analyses include within-task contrasts among decision conditions (preferred, even, worst) rather than only task>baseline contrasts, satisfying the requirement for at least one decision-making condition contrast. Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level statistical maps were generated and reported (LME voxelwise tests, cluster correction, tables/figures of significant clusters), meeting the whole-brain evidence criterion. Participant groups (occasional stimulant users) are acceptable per eligibility. Results are reported in the main text and tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to task>rest only, not PET, not ROI-only, and include whole-brain task activation maps. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans that used the Cups task (risky decision-making) during fMRI (meets I4). The paper reports within-task, condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., ADV Risk > DIS Risk and other EV contrasts) that directly compare decision-making conditions (meets I5). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise FLAME results with cluster correction and reported activation tables/figures (meets I6 and I8). Participant groups (healthy adolescents and adults) are acceptable (meets I7). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; no exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Exclusion (E5): The study uses a probabilistic reinforcement-learning/episodic memory task and investigates prediction-error-related activity and memory, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked results are reported/mentioned), I7 (human participant groups qualifying by age/health), I8 (whole-brain results referenced in main/supplemental materials). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not one of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM tasks required), I5 (no accepted decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Because I4 and I5 are not satisfied, the study must be excluded under E5.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly examines risky decision making using a framing task (sure vs gamble under gain/loss frames) with healthy human participants. It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., the framing-effect interaction: (Gsure + Lgamble) − (Ggamble + Lsure) and its reverse), and uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample t tests, whole-brain regression, cluster correction, and tables of activations). Behavioral and imaging results, methods, and discussion are present in the provided full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion), and activation results are presented in tables/figures. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., contrasts are not only vs implicit baseline, not PET, task is a risky decision-making paradigm, whole-brain results are reported, and it is an empirical report). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human adolescents performing the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (a risky decision-making paradigm) during scanning, with within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (pump decisions following negative feedback/explosion vs following positive feedback/cash-out). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (tables of coordinates, cluster-corrected maps, NeuroVault link). Participant sample and methods (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study involves human subjects performing a perceptual decision-making task (face detection) and reports group-level, whole-brain statistical maps and coordinates. However, the reported task contrasts are primarily task-versus-baseline maps and correlations of BOLD with reaction time; the paper does not present a within-task condition contrast of decision difficulty (e.g., hard > easy or low-coherence > high-coherence) or an explicit perceptual task > active control contrast that yielded significant voxelwise results. Although analyses testing stimulus variability were performed, they yielded no significant condition-vs-condition effects. Therefore the study’s decision-related analyses are effectively limited to task>baseline and parametric/RT correlations, which falls under exclusion criterion E3 (only contrasts against an implicit baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI with human perceptual DM), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps reported), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/coords). Inclusion criterion I5 (required condition-vs-condition or task>active-control contrast such as hard>easy) is not satisfied. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study does not meet the review's scope for decision-making under risk/ambiguity/perceptual uncertainty. Although it contains whole-brain group fMRI analyses and healthy participants, the scanned tasks involve incidental reward learning (a MID-like speeded response task) and a memory test for value; the explicit risky gamble manipulation (Experiment 4) was behavioral only (not scanned). Therefore key inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis are not met: no fMRI scan during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task (I4), and no qualifying decision-making contrast such as risky>safe or ambiguous>non-ambiguous (I5). Exclusion criterion E5 applies (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task). Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study in which human participants performed a risky decision-making task (Gain vs Loss trials) during whole-brain BOLD acquisition. The authors model a trial-by-trial parametric regressor (‘Gamble Risk’) and report within-task contrasts (risk parametric effects, Valence: Gain > Loss comparisons and related interactions), as well as ON vs OFF medication and group interactions. Imaging analyses are whole-brain (SPM5) with FDR correction and results are described in the text/tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>baseline only, not a review). Therefore the study satisfies the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making and provides whole-brain contrasts suitable for meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a canonical risky decision-making task. The authors report within-task parametric contrasts indexing risk (parametric modulation by pump number; effectively high-risk > low-risk) and include control pump events (white balloons) to account for motor/visual activity. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (FLAME1; voxelwise Z>2.3, cluster p<0.05 corrected). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets the review’s inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

The study reports fMRI during a risk-sensitivity decision-making task (choices between larger risky vs smaller certain rewards), and presents within-task contrasts (categorical regressors for selecting the variable/risky option versus not, and parametric subjective value regressors). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (thresholded and cluster-corrected) and ROI analyses are also described. Participants are healthy young adults and results are fully described across methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (within-task decision contrasts such as variable/risky option selected vs not, and value-related regressors), I6 (group-level whole-brain maps), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not limited to task>baseline contrasts only; includes condition contrasts and parametric effects; not PET; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level activation maps (I6) and includes participant groups that are acceptable for the review (patients and controls; I7). Whole-brain results are clearly described in the text/tables (I8). However, the task is a probabilistic reversal-learning/reward-learning paradigm and the reported contrasts are feedback-related (negative vs positive feedback; final reversal vs reversal error; final reversal error vs correct), not the decision-making contrasts required by the meta-analysis (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy). Therefore it does not satisfy inclusion criterion I5 (required decision-making contrasts). It also does not unambiguously meet I4 as a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making manipulation per the meta-analysis definitions. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are directly triggered, but because not all inclusion criteria are met (notably I5 and I4), the study is excluded.

The full text describes a human fMRI study in which participants performed a two-choice prediction decision-making task with manipulated error rates (20% reward, 50% uncertainty, 80% punishment) and an interoceptive breathing-load. The paper reports within-task condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., 50% uncertainty > 20% reward) and group × condition effects. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (LME per voxel with cluster correction) and results are reported across the whole brain (tables/figures). Participants include healthy controls and substance-using groups. The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E3–E9).

This study reports fMRI in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face vs. house categorization) during scanning (I4). It includes within-task contrasts (face>house and house>face) and analyzes effects of stimulus difficulty (three noise levels), effectively providing decision-related condition comparisons (analogous to hard>easy) and modulatory analyses by noise (I5). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM8 with second-level one-sample t-tests and whole-brain activation maps/coordinates reported (I6). Participant sample is healthy adults (I7). Whole-brain results are reported in figures/tables and described in the text (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are not limited to task>rest only, it is fMRI (not PET), includes whole-brain results (not ROI-only or only connectivity), and is empirical. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making contrasts and whole-brain reporting and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study reports simultaneous EEG/fMRI in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (Mooney image categorization). The authors conducted EEG-informed whole-brain GLM fMRI analyses with condition comparisons (objects vs. scrambled/inverted faces) and direct contrasts (HF>LF, LF>HF) and report group-level, voxelwise statistical maps with cluster correction and a table of peak coordinates (Table 1). Thus it includes fMRI during a perceptual decision task (I4), contains condition contrasts suitable for perceptual-DM (I5), provides whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation maps (I6), uses an eligible participant group (I7), and reports coordinates/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore include.

The paper reports an fMRI gambling decision-making task that manipulates uncertainty (Win vs Lose blocks) in human participants, providing within-task contrasts (Lose vs Win) and a group-level repeated-measures GLM whole-brain analysis with coordinates and statistical maps. It thus meets I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (within-task contrast: high uncertainty/lose vs low uncertainty/win), I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported), I7 (human participant groups—GAD and healthy controls are acceptable), and I8 (results reported with coordinates/figures). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not task>baseline only, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without whole-brain activation, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (Roulette Betting Task). It includes within-task contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (active-choice vs no-choice) and parametric modulators of probability and bet size, and reports group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses including whole-brain results (in addition to ROI analyses). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, rest-baseline-only contrasts) apply. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This is an fMRI study (human participants) that implemented a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion) and directly contrasts difficulty levels (hard [low coherence] vs easy [high coherence]). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (interaction of difficulty and time; ROI selection with leave-one-out; whole-brain maps and tables), satisfying requirements for a within-task contrast (hard > easy / low coherence > high coherence). Participants are healthy adults. Results are presented in full article text with methods, results, tables, and figures (whole-brain maps and coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts, empirical fMRI with appropriate contrasts).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants using a perceptual detection decision-making task (animal detection) and reports within-task condition contrasts (Pos > Neut-P and Neg > Neut-N) that directly compare decision-making conditions. Group-level, whole-brain second-level analyses are reported (FWE-corrected clusters, coordinates provided) alongside ROI analyses. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and none of the listed exclusion criteria apply.

This is a human fMRI study in healthy adults performing a card gambling task manipulating risk (six risk levels). The analysis included within-task contrasts across risk levels (e.g., low-risk vs high-risk; regressors for each risk level; control > ketanserin contrasts for low-risk negative outcomes) meeting the risky-DM contrast formats. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed in SPM5 with FWE cluster correction and coordinates reported. Thus the study satisfies: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making), I5 (condition contrasts comparing risk levels), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met: contrasts are condition-versus-condition rather than only task>baseline, modality is fMRI (not PET), task is risky decision-making (not an excluded decision type), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and task activation maps (not only connectivity or only between-group contrasts) are provided. Full text is complete and includes methods, results and discussion.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human subjects that manipulated reward probability/uncertainty (slot machines A–D) during task performance and reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., Delay Slot_B > Delay Slot_A: high uncertainty > lower uncertainty). Group-level whole-brain, random-effects SPM analyses are reported with coordinate tables and figures. Contrasts correspond to ambiguous/risky decision-making comparisons (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study uses the Iowa Gambling Task (IGT) during scanning (I4 satisfied) and reports a task>control contrast (IGT > non-gambling control) (I5 satisfied). However, all reported neuroimaging analyses were restricted to an anatomically defined VMPFC region (ROI-based analyses); the paper does not present a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or unmasked whole-brain results. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criterion I6 (whole-brain evidence) is not met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Hence EXCLUDED due to E6.

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reversal-learning task probing cognitive flexibility and feedback processing, not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the meta-analysis. Although the paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps and figures/tables (I6, I8) and includes healthy human participants (I7), it does not employ an accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM paradigm or contrasts (e.g., 'risky > safe', 'ambiguity > non-ambiguous', 'hard > easy'). Therefore inclusion criteria I4 and I5 are not met. This meets exclusion criterion E5 (task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in humans that manipulated sexual risk (high vs low) while participants made decisions about likelihood of having sex, constituting a risky decision-making task. The study reports a within-task contrast comparing risk conditions (low > high), performs a group-level whole-brain SPM analysis with voxelwise results and Talairach coordinates, and provides full Methods, Results, and Discussion. Participants are healthy adult women. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for (I4) fMRI during a risky decision-making task, (I5) at least one decision-condition contrast (high vs low risk), (I6) whole-brain group-level statistical maps reported, (I7) acceptable participant group, and (I8) whole-brain results reported in text/tables. The full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>rest only, not non-empirical). The contrast direction (low>high) still represents a valid within-task risk condition comparison and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that manipulates outcome uncertainty in a decision task (2-choice certain vs 4-choice uncertain reversal learning). It includes a within-subject contrast that directly tests uncertainty effects (4-choice > 2-choice) on responses to unexpected non-reinforcement relative to expected reinforcement, which maps onto ambiguous decision-making contrasts (high uncertainty > low uncertainty). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise (FSL/FEAT; Z-thresholding and cluster correction), and results are reported as coordinate tables and figures. Thus inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not ROI-only; not baseline-only contrasts; not connectivity-only; not non-empirical; includes within-task condition contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

The study used fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning (gambling-like) task but the reported contrasts are reward > punishment, punishment > reward, and final reversal error > baseline. None of the contrasts correspond to the required risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making comparisons (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy) required by inclusion criterion I5. The paper does provide group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports coordinates/tables, and it clearly describes the task and methods. However, because it lacks an eligible decision-making contrast quantifying risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty, it does not meet I5 and is therefore excluded.

This study meets the meta-analysis objectives and inclusion criteria: it used fMRI while participants performed the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (a risky decision-making task) (I4). The authors modeled and reported parametric modulation by explosion probability (high-risk vs low-risk) for Inflate and Success events and reported activations for these modulators across groups, providing a risk-related contrast consistent with I5. Analyses were whole-brain, voxelwise, random-effects group-level maps with cluster correction, satisfying I6. Participant group (schizophrenia and healthy controls) is an acceptable sample (I7). Whole-brain results are reported in the text and supplementary material (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/ connectivity-only, and within-group task effects (including parametric risk modulation) are reported rather than only between-group contrasts. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a within-subject fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probability-discounting risky choice task during scanning (meets I4). The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts indexing decision variables (subjective value, decision conflict) and presents decision-conflict effects (equivalent to hard > easy) and value-related contrasts (meets I5). Analyses were conducted and reported at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise SPM random-effects analyses with thresholds and clusters reported (meets I6). Participants are healthy adult males (meets I7). Whole-brain results are reported in text, tables, and figures (meets I8). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; sufficient detail is present to assess eligibility. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a probabilistic reversal learning (reward-guided) decision-making task with uncertain probabilistic outcomes. It reports within-task contrasts (exploratory vs exploitative trials; model-based prediction-error regressors PEDU/PESU) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (FWE-corrected maps and peak coordinates). The task involves probabilistic reward contingencies (80/20) and adaptive decision-making under uncertainty, fitting the review’s risky/ambiguous decision-making domain. therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not rely solely on implicit baseline contrasts, is not PET, reports whole-brain task activations (not ROI-only), and includes within-group task effects. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment in which human participants performed a delayed matching-to-sample (perceptual) decision-making task (checking task) during scanning. It includes at least one within-task decision-making contrast (decision-making followed by checking behavior (DFCB+) > decision-making not followed by checking behavior (DFCB−)), reported as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM random-effects, FDR-corrected). Participant groups (OCD patients and healthy controls) are acceptable. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, imaging acquisition, preprocessing and statistics), Results (whole-brain and ROI analyses) and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>baseline-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI contrasts.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making (card-guessing/betting) task. The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., self-selected vs. computer-selected trials; previous win vs. loss; interactions) at the group level, with whole-brain voxelwise analyses and coordinates/tables. The task and contrasts map onto risky decision-making contrasts and satisfy the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete for screening.

This study reports task fMRI in human participants performing a risky multi-step gambling decision-making task (Goal-Instructed Gambling task). It includes within-task condition contrasts that directly compare decision states (quota-severity and strategy-optimization contrasts, e.g., Imp>High>Low>Easy and Low/High>Non/Imp), and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses with cluster-size correction and peak coordinates (dlPFC, dACC, AI, dmPFC). Results include within-task contrasts and ROI/correlation follow-ups, and the full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not only baseline contrasts, not ROI-only, not only connectivity, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (animal detection) with within-task motivational manipulation (motivated vs neutral) — addressing I4 and providing a condition-versus-condition contrast (motivated > neutral) that qualifies as a decision-making contrast (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (second-level random-effects, whole-brain FWE-corrected results) satisfying I6.
