Participant groups (medicated schizophrenia patients and healthy controls) are acceptable per I7. Results are described in full text (tables/coordinates and ROI follow-ups), meeting I8. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., contrasts are not only versus implicit baseline, whole-brain maps are provided, not connectivity-only). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a probabilistic reward-learning task (Salience Attribution Test) that manipulates reward probability (high vs low) and includes ambiguous 50% probability conditions. It reports within-task condition contrasts (adaptive reward prediction: high-probability cues > low-probability cues; aberrant reward prediction: subjective high > low on task-irrelevant 50% cues) and random-effects, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected results and stereotactic coordinates. The task therefore probes decision-making under risk/uncertainty and ambiguity, the contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not baseline), and whole-brain group maps are reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4, I5, I6, I7, I8. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (sparse vs dense categorization with an uncertainty opt-out), includes within-task condition contrasts (e.g., uncertainty > correct categorization, correct > uncertainty, and parametric distance-to-bound modulators corresponding to difficulty/hard>easy), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps with coordinates and cluster statistics. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies fMRI during perceptual decision-making (I4), includes relevant condition-vs-condition contrasts (I5), provides whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps (I6), has an eligible participant group (I7), and reports whole-brain results in text/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are met. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion E3 applies: the fMRI contrast of interest reported is decision > fixation (task > rest/fixation), and the paper does not report a condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrast (e.g., risky>safe). Met inclusion criteria: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task — modified Iowa Gambling Task), I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise mapping was performed via MEPM), I7 (participant groups acceptable — substance-dependent and controls), and I8 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables). Not met: I5 (no qualifying decision-vs-decision or task-vs-active-control contrast; the primary reported contrast is against fixation). Because E3 excludes studies whose only decision-making contrasts are against an implicit baseline/rest/fixation, this study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite having whole-brain analyses. Full text appears complete and was used for screening.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult humans performing a risky decision-making task (hypothetical treatment choices with explicit side-effect probabilities and efficacies). The authors report within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (mild > severe and severe > mild side-effect conditions), perform group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses, and present corrected peak coordinates and figures (FWE-corrected). Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. These elements satisfy the review’s requirements for risky decision-making fMRI contrasts and whole-brain group results. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only reporting) are met.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in human participants performing a two-choice prediction decision-making task with three manipulated error-rate conditions (20%, 50%, 80%). The main contrasts compare error-rate conditions (e.g., 20% vs 80%), meeting the requirement for a within-task decision-making contrast (analogous to high- vs low-uncertainty). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and cluster-corrected results are reported (voxelwise thresholding, cluster size, Talairach labels; Table 3, figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Participant groups (stimulant users and controls) are appropriate per inclusion criteria, and whole-text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest only, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts) apply. Therefore the study fits the meta-analysis scope of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making and should be included.

This study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: it used fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (two-choice monetary risk-taking), explicitly tested contrasts comparing decision conditions (risky > safe and related contrasts), and reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (cluster-corrected results, tables, and figures). Participant groups (alcohol-dependent patients and matched controls) are acceptable per inclusion criteria. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, fMRI acquisition, whole-brain analysis), Results (within- and between-group contrasts, cumulative-earnings modulation), and Discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts) are met.

Although the study employed fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Iowa Gambling Task) and reports a risky > safe contrast, all reported fMRI analyses were conducted using an a priori ROI approach with small-volume corrections. The paper does not present unmasked, group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I6) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only reporting). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during risky decision-making) and I5 (risky > safe contrast) and I7 (participant groups acceptable). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (whole-brain voxelwise group maps). Full text is complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (Gabor orientation discrimination) with on-trial subjective certainty ratings. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts directly comparing decision conditions (correct-unsure vs correct-sure; correct > error), which correspond to high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty / perceptual difficulty contrasts. Whole-brain group analyses (FLAME1) and cluster-corrected maps are reported in text, tables, and figures. Participants are within the eligible population. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task vs rest-only, and not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (dynamically adaptive motion prediction). The authors report within-task condition contrasts (errors with negative feedback vs correct trials with positive feedback), which reflect comparisons between decision-making conditions (errors correspond to more difficult/uncertain perceptual decisions), satisfying the requirement for a decision-making contrast. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (voxel-wise one-sample t tests, z-maps, tables/figures), and coordinates/activations are provided. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human adolescent females that implements a decision-making task with explicit risk manipulation (high-risk vs low-risk sexual decisions) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts. The manuscript includes within-task contrasts (high-risk > low-risk and Boys (high-low) vs. control conditions), reports whole-brain cluster results in tables and figures (voxel p<.001, cluster extent threshold), and provides full methods and results. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment in which healthy human participants performed a risky decision-making task (lotteries) inside the scanner. The authors performed group-level GLM analyses including parametric modulators (ΔU, ΔMin, ΔEV), compared task conditions (Self vs Other; Comp filler), and report whole-brain activation results (with summary tables) and ROI analyses. Thus it provides within-task contrasts/parametric task effects relevant to risk decision-making, and includes group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) results. Participants are healthy university students. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI or connectivity results, contrasts only vs baseline) apply. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

This is an fMRI study in humans that used two-choice perceptual decision-making tasks (numerical and verbal) during scanning, with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses linking task activation to behavioral parameters. The paper reports between-task comparisons (numerical vs. verbal) and task-related contrasts, and performs whole-brain random-effects analyses and multiple-regression voxelwise maps (thresholded and reported with coordinates). The task is a perceptual decision-making paradigm and whole-brain results are reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI, only baseline contrasts without task-vs-task comparisons) are met. Full article text including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is present, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an fMRI study that used a risky decision-making task (modified Iowa Gambling Task) with contrasts comparing decision > no-decision and risky > safe. Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level analyses were performed (SPM2) with FWE-corrected maps reported and ANCOVA group comparisons. Participant groups (controls, substance-dependent, substance-dependent with gambling) are acceptable. The manuscript includes full methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic multi-cue decision-making task that manipulates uncertainty and time pressure. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses (parametric modulation by subjective and objective sum of evidence, phase contrasts HighP>LowP, conjunctions) with corrected voxelwise cluster results and tables of clusters. Task contrasts compare decision conditions (low vs high time pressure) and parametric contrasts indexing uncertainty/evidence (high vs low SoE), satisfying condition-vs-condition contrasts relevant to risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study reports an event-related fMRI investigation of risky decision-making in humans (children, adolescents, adults) using a gambling task. It includes the explicit risky > sure (Risky Bet > Sure Bet) contrast, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction, and presents whole-brain results in the text, tables and figures. Participants are healthy human subjects across allowed age ranges. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, only ROI, only baseline contrasts, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that administered a perceptual decision-making task (visual motion direction discrimination) during task fMRI and reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps. The authors modelled parametric effects of motion coherence (20/40/80%) across trials, providing within-task contrasts equivalent to perceptual-DM comparisons (e.g., low-coherence/hard vs high-coherence/easy via parametric modulation). Task-related whole-brain group analyses (cluster-level FWE-corrected maps) and peak coordinates are reported. Participants are healthy humans. Although the paper emphasizes resting-state connectivity, the presence of whole-brain task activation maps and appropriate within-task contrasts meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants that manipulated ambiguity in a decision-making task (ambiguous, unambiguous, incongruent sequences) and implicitly biased choices. The paper reports within-task condition contrasts including ambiguous > unambiguous and ambiguous > incongruent, and order (2-1 > 1-2) contrasts that directly compare decision-making conditions (matches ambiguous-DM contrast types). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with FWE cluster correction and reported coordinates/parameter estimates. Participants are healthy adults. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants using a risky decision-making task (modified Iowa Gambling Task) with within-task contrasts (bad deck > good deck; framed vs control risk effects). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FDR-corrected maps and peak coordinates), and results are presented as whole-brain statistical maps/coordinates. Participant groups include substance-dependent and non-substance-dependent individuals (eligible per I7). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not only ROI/connectivity, not task>rest only, includes within-group contrasts). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This study used fMRI during a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task and reports whole-brain, group-level contrasts of feedback-related activation and cycle-phase interactions, but it does not present any of the required decision-making contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy) specified by the meta-analysis. Instead, reported contrasts are feedback-based (positive vs negative) and cycle-phase interactions. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (required decision-making contrast) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision-related task), I6 (whole-brain group-level analyses), I7 (participant group acceptable — healthy humans), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making contrasts). No exclusion criteria from the provided list were directly triggered; exclusion is based on failure to meet all inclusion criteria (I5). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study (BART during scan) meets I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task) and I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported) and I8 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures/text). However, it does not present a qualifying condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrast as required by I5. The reported analyses appear to be condition > implicit baseline contrasts (e.g., pumps/cash-outs modeled against the implicit baseline) and age regressions on these condition maps; there is no clear “risky > safe”, “high-risk > low-risk”, “pump > cash-out”, or other within-task risky-vs-safe or task-vs-control contrast presented. Because the study’s decision-making contrasts are only against an implicit baseline, it meets exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore I exclude the study from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using the Balloon Analog Risk Task (risky decision-making) administered during scanning, with parametric modulators of explosion probability (i.e., high-risk > low-risk type contrasts). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses are reported with cluster-corrected results and stereotactic coordinates; within-group task effects (one-sample t-tests in healthy men) and between-group contrasts are provided. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion. Therefore it meets the review’s fMRI risky-DM task requirement and provides whole-brain condition-vs-condition contrasts and coordinates.

This is an fMRI study in humans using a monetary probability task (cues with 0,25,50,75,100% chance) that manipulates decision-making under risk/uncertainty. The authors report within-subject condition contrasts (linear contrasts across five expectation conditions and outcome regressors contrasting positive vs negative prediction error), computed at the group (second) level with voxelwise SPM analyses and whole-brain FWE correction. Participants are healthy humans and whole-brain results are described in text/tables. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8).

The study reports whole-brain fMRI results from a two-step sequential reinforcement-learning task and provides group-level voxelwise contrasts (model-based vs model-free prediction-error regressors) and full methods/results/discussion. However, the meta-analysis specifically targets risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks. The two-step task is a model-based/model-free reinforcement-learning paradigm and does not constitute a risky, ambiguity, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review; therefore it fails the task-domain inclusion criterion. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (does not report contrasts in the specified risky/ambiguous/perceptual forms). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study (Experiment 4) in which healthy human participants performed a risky decision-making task (accept/reject lotteries). The paper reports within-task contrasts (e.g., gain > loss; accept > reject) and parametric contrasts for risk (variance) and EV, and tests interactions—i.e., condition-versus-condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM8 results with cluster-level FWE correction, and coordinates/tables of activations are provided. Participants are healthy adults. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (condition contrasts such as gain>loss, risk parametric effects), I6 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/text). No exclusion criteria are met (not a PET-only, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>baseline-only). Full text is complete. Therefore INCLUDE for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study used the Balloon Analog Risk Task (BART) during whole-brain, group-level SPM analyses to examine covariance between risk level (parametric modulation of explosion probability) and brain activation, comparing post-win vs post-loss decision events. It reports voxelwise random-effects analyses (2x2 ANOVA) with whole-brain cluster correction and within-group maps, satisfying the requirement for condition-versus-condition contrasts (risk-level parametric effects and after-loss vs after-win comparisons). Participants are human adolescents (IGD and HCs). Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making contrasts and whole-brain reporting.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing an ecologically valid risky decision-making task (virtual sexual ‘hook up’ game) during scanning (meets I4). It reports condition-vs-condition contrasts including SRD > Conversational (an active control) and SRD > implicit baseline (meets I5). Group-level voxelwise/statistical maps and TFCE cluster results with peak coordinates are reported for task contrasts and between-group comparisons (reported clusters/coordinates and whole-brain covariate analyses), satisfying whole-brain, group-level reporting (I6) and coordinate reporting (I8). Participant sample (MSM, including meth users and non-users) is an acceptable participant group (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: contrasts are not only against implicit baseline (E3 not met), not PET (E4), task is risky decision-making (E5 not met), whole-brain results/coordinates are reported (E6 not met), and this is empirical fMRI activation (E7, E8 not met). Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing perceptual decision-making tasks (criterion comparison and signal detection) with explicit manipulations of difficulty/uncertainty (easy vs difficult; varying coherence/signal level). The authors report group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM and searchlight MVPA results (voxelwise analyses, cluster-corrected) and provide Talairach coordinates and figures. Contrasts compare decision conditions (parametric uncertainty modulation; difficult>easy/low coherence>high coherence-type effects) and include a task versus active control (categorization vs letter-identification) analysis. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8). No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, not only baseline contrasts, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study used human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (detecting short vs long digit sequences with implicit cues) manipulating uncertainty; it reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts comparing conditions (e.g., high vs low uncertainty checkpoints) and prediction-error contrasts (TERM>EXT, CHECK_HIGH>CHECK_LOW), with thresholding and cluster correction. Behavioral and fMRI methods, results and discussion are present in full text. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during decision-making task of perceptual nature), I5 (condition contrasts such as CHECK_HIGH>CHECK_LOW, TERM>EXT), I6 (group whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria met: E3-E9 not applicable. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study acquired whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps while participants performed a probabilistic classification task (weather prediction task) with uncertainty/predictive-value manipulations and an explicit control task. The methods report whole-brain random-effects analyses and tables of coordinates for task-related activations (presentation and feedback phases) and within-group task activations, satisfying the requirement for task-versus-control and condition-versus-condition contrasts related to uncertainty/predictive value. Participants include stroke patients and controls (eligible participant groups). Results are reported as whole-brain maps and coordinate tables. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI of ambiguous/risky/perceptual decision-making and provides whole-brain, group-level results.

This study collected fMRI during a risky decision-making task (satisfies I4) but does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) activation map for a decision-making contrast (e.g., risky > safe, risk > certainty, hard > easy) required by the meta-analysis. The reported fMRI whole-brain results pertain to outcome-phase contrasts (human > computer) and PPI connectivity maps; decision-related analyses are reported primarily as ROI-based univariate tests, MVPA restricted to anatomically-defined ROIs, and seed-based PPI connectivity. Thus the study lacks an unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise decision-making contrast needed to meet I5 and I6. Inclusion criteria met: I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6. No exclusion criteria from the provided list are strictly triggered (exclusion_criteria_applied=[]). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study reports an fMRI experiment in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (sequential ‘boxes’ gamble). Analyses include within-task contrasts and parametric modulators (e.g., magnitude of missed opportunity; loss position) and second-level random-effects, voxelwise, whole-brain SPM8 analyses with multiple-comparison correction and reported peak coordinates/figures. Participants are healthy adults. Contrasts are condition-versus-condition/parametric (not only task>baseline). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the paper satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study includes a probabilistic discounting (PD) task that is a risky decision-making paradigm (choices between sure €20 and probabilistic rewards), and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (parametric subjective-value regressors) with coordinates and statistical maps. The PD analysis provides within-task contrasts (subjective value correlation for probabilistic options) that constitute a decision-making effect appropriate for risky-DM meta-analysis. The full text contains methods, results, and figures/tables documenting whole-brain results (with SVC reported but based on group-level voxelwise maps). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state, and it includes within-task task effects rather than only baseline contrasts. Although the paper also includes delay-discounting (an excluded task type), the presence of a qualifying risky (probability) task and whole-brain PD contrasts satisfies inclusion. Therefore include.

This is an fMRI study in humans performing a probabilistic (uncertain) two-step decision task with monetary outcomes (decision-making under risk/uncertainty). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected) and presents task-related contrasts/parametric modulators comparing neural responses as a function of prediction-error magnitude (high vs low SPE/RPE) and direct contrasts (e.g., SPE vs abs(RPE)). These are within-task, condition-vs-condition decision-making contrasts tied to uncertainty and hence relevant to risky/uncertain decision-making. Whole-brain results are reported in the text/tables/figures. Participants are healthy humans. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

This fMRI study had healthy human participants performing a dual-choice card gambling task that manipulated risk (high-risk vs low-risk) and used a parametric regressor for chosen risk. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were reported (SPM8) with FWE correction and whole-brain results (and ROI-constrained results) presented in tables and figures. The reported contrasts include risk-related activation scaling with risk magnitude (equivalent to high-risk > low-risk). The task and contrasts align with the review objective (risky decision-making). Full text is complete and contains methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study using a probabilistic passive-avoidance task (70% reward/punishment contingencies) that involves decision-making under uncertainty (risky decision-making). The study models decision-phase (approach vs avoid) and feedback-phase (reward/punishment) with parametric modulators (expected value and prediction error), and reports both ROI and whole-brain group-level (voxelwise) analyses (whole-brain results reported in Table 4 and main-effect analyses within the nonmaltreated group). Within-task condition contrasts (approach vs avoidance; reward vs punishment feedback; EV/PE-modulated responses) are present, satisfying the requirement for condition-vs-condition contrasts. Participants are human children (age 10–15), an acceptable participant group. The full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are met.

This study is an fMRI investigation with whole-brain analyses in healthy participants (adolescents and adults) and reports whole-brain results; however, the task is a reward-processing Card Guessing Task that the authors explicitly state is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm. Contrasts are reward vs. no-reward (reward receipt/consumption), not risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy perceptual contrasts. Therefore it fails the required scope for decision-making tasks in this review. Exclusion ID met: E5 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual). Inclusion IDs met: I6, I7, I8. Inclusion IDs not met: I4, I5.

This is an fMRI study using a gambling (risky decision-making) task with within-task contrasts (risky vs non-risky and parametric effects related to risk) and reports group-level whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with stereotactic coordinates and tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making (I4, I5), provides whole-brain voxelwise group results (I6), and participant sampling is acceptable (I7); results are reported with coordinates/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply.

This study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria: it reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a risky decision-making task (Risky Gains Task) (I4). It includes condition-vs-condition contrasts (risky vs safe decisions) and reports group-by-decision analyses (risky > safe / risky vs safe contrasts are analyzed) (I5). Second-level, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction (AlphaSim) are performed and reported (I6). Participant groups include substance-using and comparison subjects, which are acceptable (I7). Whole-brain results are reported in text/figures/tables (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to baseline contrasts, not PET, not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, and the report includes within-task condition contrasts rather than only between-group effects. The provided full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study in human adolescents using the HiLo decision-making task that manipulates uncertainty (pure uncertainty 50% vs probabilistic conditions). The primary contrast of interest is a condition-vs-condition contrast (50% condition vs other task conditions), which corresponds to an ambiguous/high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty comparison. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (FLAME) with cluster correction are reported and thresholded maps/clusters are provided in tables and figures. The task and contrasts directly address ambiguous decision-making and meet the meta-analysis requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants making risk-related decisions in driving (urgent braking vs. risk evaluation). It reports within-task condition contrasts (urgent > evaluative and vice versa) that are directly relevant to risky decision-making, uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM12, AlphaSim correction) and reports cluster coordinates/tables and figures. The tasks constitute risky decision-making (braking to avoid hazards), satisfying the meta-analysis scope. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-vs-condition (not task>baseline only), modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only or connectivity-only), and the paper is empirical. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy humans that manipulated probabilistic (risky) decision-making (Gambling blocks) and deterministic rule-based choices, and reports contrasts between decision conditions (e.g., low vs. high choice certainty; complex rule-based vs. high-certainty probabilistic). Group-level voxelwise analyses and activation foci are reported (tables and SPM analyses), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The task and contrasts directly address risky/probabilistic decision-making relevant to the review. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a probabilistic classification task that manipulates uncertainty (entropy) — an ambiguous decision-making paradigm. The paper includes condition-vs-condition and parametric contrasts relevant to decision-making (e.g., negative feedback vs positive feedback, and BOLD correlated with increasing entropy/high vs low uncertainty). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (SPM99 second-level analyses, with FDR and cluster corrections), and coordinates/tables are provided. Although the entropy effect was significant within a predefined midbrain ROI rather than surviving whole-brain correction, the study did perform whole-brain analyses and reports whole-brain results for other contrasts, and therefore meets the meta-analysis requirements. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present and complete in the provided content.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that used an experiential risky decision-making task (choices between sure and risky monetary options). The paper reports within-task contrasts and model-based regressors (e.g., RSTD prediction error; contrasts comparing risk-related trials to other trials) and performs a group-level, whole-brain, random-effects analysis with familywise error correction, reporting surviving clusters and coordinates (Table 1). The full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I4 (fMRI risky decision task), I5 (within-task decision-making contrasts/model regressors), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (participant group acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (face/house discrimination) meeting the review scope. It collected BOLD data while human subjects performed a perceptual decision task (I4). The paper reports within-task contrasts and condition comparisons (face vs house, analyses across noise/difficulty and RT bins), satisfying the requirement for at least one decision-vs-decision or difficulty contrast (I5). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (repeated-measures ANOVA, voxelwise GLM) with reported peak coordinates and ROI maps, fulfilling whole-brain evidence (I6) and acceptable reporting formats (I8). Participant group (healthy young adults) is acceptable under participant criteria (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not only task>baseline (E3), not PET (E4), are perceptual DM (not excluded by E5), include whole-brain results (not E6), are not connectivity-only (not E7), and are empirical data (not E9). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports an fMRI experiment in which human participants performed an ambiguous decision-making task (valence judgments of sounds with manipulated consonance/dissonance). Relevant contrasts compare ambiguous vs less-ambiguous conditions (intermediate dissonance > consonance; strong > intermediate), meeting the required condition-vs-condition contrasts for ambiguous-DM. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM second-level one-sample t-tests) are reported, with cluster and voxel-level thresholding and coordinates presented. Participants are healthy human adults. Results and coordinates are reported in text/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-task contrasts rather than only task>rest). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an fMRI study in healthy humans performing an explicit risky decision-making task (Risky-Gains Task). It includes condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., +80 vs +40 high-risk > low-risk, and regressors for safe [20] vs risky [40/80]) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (LME) with cluster-corrected results and tables of coordinates. Results are presented in the main text/tables/figures. Thus it satisfies I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (within-task decision-making contrasts: high-risk>low-risk and safe vs risky regressors), I6 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps reported), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not baseline-only contrasts, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study in humans using a gambling (risky decision-making) task with manipulated winning probabilities. The paper reports within-task contrasts (decision-for-self vs decision-for-other), parametric modulation of decision value, and whole-brain, group-level GLM results with reported voxel coordinates and cluster maps. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition/analysis), Results, and Discussion, allowing assessment of eligibility. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making: (I4) fMRI during risky DM task, (I5) at least one condition-vs-condition decision contrast (self vs other and parametric value contrasts), (I6) whole-brain group-level maps reported, (I7) acceptable participant group (healthy adults), and (I8) whole-brain results are reported in text/figures. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study reports fMRI data collected while participants performed a probability discounting task (probability option vs fixed/certain option), which is a risky decision-making paradigm. The paper includes within-task contrasts (probability > fixed) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8 second-level analyses with cluster correction) and reports brain regions/coordinates. Although the study also includes delay-discounting (intertemporal) tasks (which would be excluded), the presence of the probability discounting task satisfies the review’s requirement for a risky decision-making fMRI contrast. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, or reporting only between-group contrasts) are met. Full text contains Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore it meets I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 and is includable in the meta-analysis.

Exclusion: E5 applies. This study’s reported fMRI contrast is Win > No Win (reward receipt vs no reward) from the feedback phase, which is reward receipt without an uncertainty manipulation and not a decision-phase contrast comparing risk levels. Inclusion: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task) is satisfied because the Wheel of Fortune is a risky-DM paradigm; I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps) is satisfied — whole-brain ANCOVA results are reported; I7 (participant group acceptable) is satisfied; I8 (results reported in text/tables/figures) is satisfied. Inclusion not met: I5 is not met — the paper does not report a decision-making contrast of interest for the meta-analysis (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, or risk > certainty); the only analyzed/ reported contrast isolates reward receipt (Win > No Win) across all trial types. Therefore the study should be excluded from the decision-making meta-analysis.

This fMRI study collected whole-brain, group-level task-evoked data while human participants performed a probabilistic reward-guided decision-making task with uncertain/anti-correlated reward contingencies and reversals. The task involves decision-making under probabilistic uncertainty (risk/ambiguity) and includes within-task condition contrasts (reward vs. punishment; positive vs. negative prediction error parametric modulators) and PE-related contrasts used in whole-brain analyses. Results are reported as voxelwise group-level maps with coordinates and FWE correction. Participant groups (alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls) are acceptable. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (spatial-frequency discrimination), satisfying I4. The analysis includes within-task contrasts of task difficulty using parametric modulation (equivalent to hard>easy/low coherence>high coherence) and generates contrast images of modulation by difficulty, satisfying I5. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed in SPM12 with FWE correction and reported MNI coordinates, satisfying I6 and I8. Participant groups (younger and older healthy adults) are acceptable per I7. No exclusion criteria apply: the study does not rely only on baseline contrasts (E3), is not PET (E4), addresses perceptual DM (not excluded by E5), reports whole-brain results rather than only ROI or connectivity (E6, E7), and is empirical (not E9). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in human healthy adults using a risky decision-making task (the Cups task) with immediate feedback. It reports task contrasts of interest (e.g., Risky > Safe and Win > Loss), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-based correction, and provides coordinates and figures for significant activations. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (relevant decision-making contrasts such as risky > safe), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I7 (acceptable participant group: healthy adults), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This empirical paper reports multiple fMRI experiments in which human participants made risky/ambiguous decisions (probability-weighting and regret experiments using probabilistic electric-shock lotteries and choice among lotteries/doors). The manuscript reports within-subject condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., different probabilities; high-regret > no-regret; rejoice vs regret interactions) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and tables of regions. Participants are healthy adults. Although the chapter also summarizes an intertemporal (dread) experiment (intertemporal choice is excluded if sole focus), the presence of the probability-weighting and regret experiments provides direct risky/ambiguous decision-making contrasts suitable for the meta-analysis. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for methods and results reporting relevant contrasts.

Exclusion E5 applies: the task is an instruction-based learning/outcome-integration paradigm, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as required. Inclusion met: I6 (group-level whole-brain contrast maps were computed), I7 (healthy human participants), I8 (whole-brain results and coordinates described). Inclusion not met: I4 (the task is not a decision-making task under risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty), I5 (no appropriate decision-making contrast such as ambiguous > non-ambiguous or risky > safe was reported). Full text appears complete for screening.

This fMRI study examines social approach/avoid judgment of facial expressions (social decision-making about ambiguous stimuli). Although it meets multiple inclusion criteria for the review (I4: fMRI during an ambiguous decision-making task; I5: contains a decision-making task versus an active control task contrast — social judgment > sex discrimination; I6: reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses; I7: uses an eligible participant group [healthy adults]; I8: whole-brain results are reported in text/figures), it must be excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E5. The task is explicitly social decision-making (approach/avoid), which the review’s exclusion criteria list as not qualifying (e.g., moral or social decision-making is excluded). No other exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reversal learning (PRL) task, a decision-making paradigm involving choices under probabilistic uncertainty (risk). It reports within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (e.g., lose-shift vs. win-stay; lose-stay vs. win-stay; lose-shift vs. lose-stay) that index decision processes and feedback-driven choice, satisfying the requirement for a contrast between decision-making conditions. Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistics (Monte Carlo-corrected thresholds) and report whole-brain results and ROI correlations. Participant groups (schizophrenia patients and controls) are acceptable per inclusion rules. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record appears complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., task>rest only, PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts) are met.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (face gender categorization) with manipulation of stimulus coherence (phase noise) and morphing to change difficulty. It reports within-task contrasts comparing noise-present (low coherence) versus noise-absent (higher coherence) and versus control, matching perceptual-DM contrasts (e.g., low coherence > high coherence). Whole-brain, group-level random-effects fMRI analyses are reported with stereotactic coordinates (Table 1) and conjunctions; ROI analyses are supplemental but do not replace whole-brain maps. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in which human participants performed a probabilistic (stochastic) classification task (weather prediction task) — a decision-making task under uncertainty (ambiguous/probabilistic). It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects, FDR-corrected) with reported Talairach coordinates and cluster tables. It contains at least one task-versus-active-control contrast (WPT > control task during presentation and feedback periods) and within-task contrasts relevant to uncertainty (high > low predictive value). Participants are healthy humans. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision task under uncertainty), I5 (task > control and within-task contrasts), I6 (whole-brain group-level maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), and I8 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, not only baseline contrasts). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in which 24 healthy human participants performed a risky decision-making task (choose gamble vs guaranteed $10) while being scanned. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected clusters) showing neural correlates of decision risk (parametric modulation of gamble variance) and other decision variables. The key contrast is a trial-by-trial parametric effect of risk (i.e., high-risk > low-risk type effect) at the time of decision, reported as whole-brain maps and peak coordinates (Tables S1, S3). Participants are healthy adults and results are reported in whole-brain activation tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest-only, and not connectivity-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, SI Methods). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social/economic (Trust Game) decision-making focused on fairness and Machiavellianism. Although it reports whole-brain, group-level task contrasts (Fair–Control, Unfair–Control) and provides voxelwise results, the task is social/moral/economic (trust/reciprocity) rather than a canonical risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm targeted by the meta-analysis. Exclusion criterion E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM — e.g., moral or social decision-making) applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task vs active control contrasts reported), I6 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I7 (eligible participant group), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as defined by the review). Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study in humans that administered a mixed gain–loss gambling task (risky decision-making) during scanning and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts of decision-related activity. The paper presents within-task contrasts (parametric modulation of decision phase by gain–loss ratio; linear and quadratic effects; within-group and between-group contrasts) rather than only task>baseline, and reports whole-brain SPM8 results with stereotactic coordinates and cluster-level inference. Participants include both pathological gamblers and healthy controls (acceptable per eligibility). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, resting-state/connectivity-only, implicit-baseline-only contrasts) are met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI risky decision-making and provides usable whole-brain activation results.

Excluded because the study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (E5). Although the paper used fMRI with group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (I6), included qualifying participant groups (ASD and controls) (I7), and reported whole-brain results in tables/figures (I8), it did not implement a decision-making task nor report contrasts that compare decision-making conditions (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, hard>easy). The fMRI contrasts are stimulation (texture) > rest (baseline) and within- and between-group texture effects, not decision-making condition-versus-condition or task-versus-active-control contrasts; thus I4 and I5 are not met. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task).

The study reports task-based whole-brain fMRI during a probabilistic reversal-learning task (PRLT) that uses explicit probabilistic feedback (80:20), i.e. decision-making under uncertainty/risk, and includes an affectively neutral active baseline control task. The authors computed within-task contrasts (monetary gain vs baseline, monetary loss vs baseline, reversal vs baseline) and performed group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM2, random effects) with whole-brain thresholding and tabulated/figured results. Participants include clinical and control groups. Thus the paper meets I4 (fMRI during risky/uncertain decision-making), I5 (experimental task > active control contrasts reported), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant groups), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; contrasts are against active control not implicit baseline; within-group task effects reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI during a monetary gambling task (risky decision-making) and therefore directly addresses the review objective. It includes within-task contrasts comparing levels of risk (a linear gambling-risk contrast and high-risk > low-risk outcome contrasts), satisfying condition-vs-condition contrast requirements. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses were performed (second-level SPM8 ANOVA) with reported cluster results and MNI coordinates and FWE correction; ROI-restricted corrections were also used but whole-brain results are present. Participant sample (healthy twins at familial risk) is an allowed subject group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered.

This is an empirical, within-subject fMRI study in healthy human participants performing an event-related gambling (guessing) task that manipulates uncertainty/risk during the anticipation phase. It reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., Anticipation $4 vs No-change; Ant $4–No-ch $4 and Ant 50c–No-ch 50c) rather than task>rest, satisfying risky/ambiguous decision contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported (SPM8, voxelwise thresholding with cluster reporting) with results presented as clusters/coordinates and parameter estimates. Participants are healthy humans in a crossover design. Therefore I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8 are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of risky decision-making (subjects bluffing in a domino game) and includes condition contrasts (nonmatch [risky] vs match [safe]) with healthy human participants. However, MRI acquisition used a small number of slices centered on the amygdala (partial brain coverage) and analyses focus on anatomically defined ROI and small-volume/group GLMs restricted to the amygdala; no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map is reported. Therefore the study does not provide whole-brain results required for inclusion and meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only / no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that includes probabilistic (risky) decision trials and directly contrasts probabilistic versus intertemporal valuation (reports R>D and D>R contrasts). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain GLM results with cluster-corrected maps and tabulated local maxima, satisfying requirements for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Although the task also includes intertemporal (delay) trials (which alone would be excluded), the presence of risky/probabilistic trials and explicit risk versus delay contrasts makes the study relevant to risky decision-making. The manuscript contains full methods, results, and discussion (full text appears complete). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, baseline-only contrasts, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical paper) apply.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion discrimination) with within-task contrasts (rewarded vs nonrewarded; directional probability contrasts). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with statistical maps and tables of coordinates, including t-maps and corrected peaks. Participants are healthy humans and full article includes methods, results, and discussion. These elements satisfy the review’s inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies and do not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants that used a perceptual decision-making task (random dot motion) during scanning and included risk/ambiguity manipulations (easy, hard, ambiguous trials and shock anticipation linked to performance). The analyses include within-task contrasts and parametric modulators relevant to perceptual decision-making (e.g., coherence modulation, a 2×2 RepHigh/RepLow × Easy/Uncertain ANOVA, and parametric conformity/dissent contrasts), and report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (SPM8 second-level random-effects analyses; FDR and SVC corrections) with coordinates/tables. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study fits the meta-analysis criteria: (1) Participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion) during fMRI (I4). (2) The paper reports within-task, condition-related contrasts using parametric modulators (coherence, trial-wise bias, and reward prediction error), which constitute decision-related contrasts (i.e., comparisons across task conditions/levels) (I5). (3) Analyses are group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise (FLAME mixed-effects) with cluster-based correction and reported statistical maps/figures (I6). (4) Participant sample are healthy adult humans within accepted age range (I7). (5) Whole-brain results are presented in figures and tables in the main text (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: this is not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, not task>baseline only, and it is an empirical fMRI study. The full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Although this study used fMRI during a risky decision-making task (Wheel of Fortune) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps, the analyses reported and emphasized in the paper are limited to the feedback/outcome phase (Win vs. No Win). The meta-analysis requires at least one contrast that compares decision-making conditions (e.g., risky > safe, high-risk > low-risk, risk > certainty) or a decision-making task vs an active control (I5). This study does not report or focus on any decision-phase contrasts of risk vs. safe (selection/choice-phase contrasts); instead the primary contrast is reward receipt vs reward absence, which is an outcome/feedback contrast rather than a decision-making contrast of interest. Therefore I5 is not met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I4 (fMRI during a risky decision-making task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I7 (acceptable participant group), I8 (results clearly described in text/figures). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) were triggered by the full text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion reason: This study conducted fMRI during a probabilistic reversal learning task (meets I4) in human participants (adolescents and adults; meets I7). However, the imaging results are reported only as ROI-based analyses (ACC, VS, vmPFC) and discrete-state summaries, with no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation maps or whole-brain coordinate tables presented; thus it qualifies as an ROI-only study (meets exclusion E6). In addition, the reported contrasts are feedback/decision condition comparisons (PFB, NFB-Stay, NFB-Switch) rather than standard risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, hard>easy), so it does not provide the required decision-making contrast form for the meta-analysis (fails I5 and I6). Therefore exclude under E6. Inclusion criteria met: I4, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It reports an fMRI scan during a risky decision-making task (Iowa Gambling Task) in human adolescents (I4). It includes explicit condition contrasts comparing high-risk versus low-risk choices (I5). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps (3×2×3 ANOVA) reported in the results and tables (I6). Participant groups (adolescents with depression/suicide attempt and healthy controls) are acceptable (I7). Whole-brain results are described in text/tables and figures (I8). No exclusion criteria are met: the contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not task>baseline), the modality is fMRI (not PET), the task is a risky decision-making task (not excluded types), whole-brain results (not only ROI or connectivity) are reported, and the paper is empirical. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study used fMRI during a rewarded antisaccade (inhibitory control) task but does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported), I7 (human participants; age groups acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (contrasts are reward vs neutral/incentive cue and preparatory/saccade epochs, not one of the admitted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the paper is excluded from the meta-analysis for not meeting I4 and I5.

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans (N=19 healthy volunteers) that manipulates perceptual uncertainty using blurred vs clear images and reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., blurred > clear; uncertainty-reducing second-picture B–C > non-reducing B–C). The analyses include third-level mixed-effects group results and whole-brain cluster-corrected maps as well as ROI results, and whole-brain findings are reported (figures/tables). Thus the study provides group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from a perceptual/ambiguous decision-making paradigm, meeting the meta-analysis scope. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis.

This study meets the review criteria. It acquired fMRI while human participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning task (decision-making under uncertainty), satisfying I4. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level task-evoked statistical maps (parametric PE regressors and group contrasts), satisfying I6 and I8. The paper includes between-condition contrasts comparing decision-making contexts (reward-seeking vs punishment-avoidance) and stimulus-domain conditions (faces vs abstract), which are valid within-task decision-making condition contrasts for the meta-analysis (satisfying I5). Participants are a healthy human sample (I7). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not only task>baseline implicit contrasts (they include between-condition contrasts and parametric contrasts), not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and not non-empirical. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore include.

This study reports an fMRI experiment (3T scanner) collected while healthy human participants performed a risky gamble decision-making task with explicit probabilities (risky > safe equivalence manipulated across trials). The authors conducted group-level, voxelwise second-level analyses and report condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., interactions of decision: gamble vs sure combined with CS effects) rather than task>rest comparisons. Whole-brain results and MNI coordinates are reported (with both an a priori amygdala mask and post-hoc whole-brain exploratory maps). Participants are healthy volunteers. Therefore the paper meets fMRI during risky decision-making (I4), contains decision-condition contrasts (I5), provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps (I6) and reports coordinates (I8), and uses an eligible participant group (I7). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete for screening.

This study reports whole-brain fMRI collected while human participants performed a probabilistic (uncertainty-manipulated) reinforcement learning task with monetary outcomes (50%, 69%, 100% predictability). The authors report voxelwise, group-level contrasts comparing decision-making conditions (predictability-related contrasts: 100%<69%<50%, within-group and between-group comparisons) with whole-brain statistical maps and tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision task with uncertainty), I5 (within-task contrasts across uncertainty levels), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is a human fMRI study in which participants performed a risky decision-making task (rating risk of physical activities) manipulating likelihood and severity. The paper reports condition-versus-condition contrasts (e.g., high-risk > low-risk; high-harm > low-harm; Risk x Format interactions) rather than only task>baseline. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results with cluster-level correction and reported peak coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all specified inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

Exclusion E5 met: the task is a probabilistic reversal-learning paradigm probing cognitive flexibility, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (fMRI during a decision/choice task), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), I7 (participant groups acceptable), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 — the study does not present any of the required decision-making contrasts (e.g., risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, or hard>easy). The reported contrasts focus on phase (acquisition vs reversal) and accuracy (correct win vs incorrect loss) and diagnostic group interactions rather than risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty contrasts. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not satisfy the meta-analysis’ required decision-making contrast types and must be excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses functional MRI while human participants performed a risky decision-making task (I4), reports task contrasts comparing decision conditions including gamble > sure (choice regressor; I5), reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with random-effects statistics and whole-brain FWE-corrected clusters and stereotactic coordinates (I6, I8), and includes an eligible participant group of healthy adults (I7). The full text includes introduction, methods (task, behavioral modeling, fMRI acquisition and GLM), results (behavioral and whole-brain imaging tables/coordinates), and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not contrasts vs implicit baseline only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky, ambiguous, and perceptual decision-making.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans using a risky decision-making task (accept/reject mixed gambles with 50% win/loss probability). The paper reports within-task, condition-vs-condition contrasts and parametric contrasts (e.g., anticipation/activation for losses vs gains, bidirectional responses, acceptance > rejection) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM8; thresholds reported). Methods, results, and discussion are fully present. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies.

This fMRI study used a probabilistic reversal learning (PRL) decision-making task with monetary feedback and modeled three feedback conditions (win, lose-stay, lose-shift) at first level and a whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analysis at second level. The authors report whole-brain group results for the lose-shift condition (FWE-corrected maps, clusters) and gPPI connectivity as supplementary analysis. The task involves uncertainty/probabilistic feedback (decision-making under uncertainty) and provides within-task condition contrasts (feedback conditions) qualifying under the review definitions. Participant groups are acceptable and results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps in the text/figures/SI. No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, baseline-only contrasts) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants (primary care physicians) performing diagnostic decision-making tasks that explicitly manipulate diagnosticity (high vs low diagnosticity → maps to certainty/uncertainty). It includes within-task condition contrasts comparing diagnostic information of differing diagnosticity and task contrasts (diagnosis vs naming; diagnosis vs prescription), matching the required contrast types (e.g., high uncertainty/low diagnosticity vs low uncertainty/high diagnosticity). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps (SPM12) with peak coordinates and FWE correction reported. Participants are an acceptable human group. Results and maps are reported in the main text and figures/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion as an ambiguous (uncertainty) decision-making fMRI study.

This is an fMRI study in humans using the probabilistic “weather prediction” task (decisions under probabilistic uncertainty), with task-versus-control contrasts (weather prediction > perceptual-motor control) and group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses reported (tables and figures). The task constitutes decision-making under uncertainty (ambiguous DM), the admitted contrast form (task > control) matches I5, whole-brain voxelwise maps and second-level analyses are present (I6), participant groups (patients and healthy adults) are acceptable (I7), and results are reported in text/tables/figures (I8). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not resting baseline contrasts only; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses fMRI during a risky decision-making game (I4) and reports within-task contrasts comparing non-match (risky) vs match (safe) anticipation and outcome contrasts (I5). Participant sample (OCD patients and controls) is acceptable (I7) and results are described in text/figures (I8). However, the paper reports task activation results primarily via region-of-interest (ROI) extractions (amygdala and nucleus accumbens) using templates from a prior study rather than presenting a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map required for inclusion (I6). Thus it meets exclusion criterion E6 (ROI-only task activation reporting without whole-brain task results). Because it does not provide the requisite group-level whole-brain task activation maps, it cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

Exclusion met: E5 - the task is a probabilistic reversal learning (reinforcement-learning) task focused on contingency learning and prediction-error signaling, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise fMRI analyses with reported coordinates and corrected cluster thresholds), I7 (participant sample falls within acceptable groups/age range), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and clearly described). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is not classified as a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm per the review definitions), I5 (the reported contrasts—punished reversal errors vs rewarded correct responses—are within a reversal-learning framework and do not match the specified risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast types). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment with 30 human subjects performing a sequential investment task involving risk (I4). The authors report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLM results: parametric modulation by model-derived TD errors (outcome phase) and Q-values (choice phase), with cluster-corrected whole-brain statistics and reported peak coordinates (satisfies I6 and I8). The analyses constitute task-related contrasts (parametric modulators tested against zero), providing condition/task-related whole-brain contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (I5). Participants are healthy adults (I7). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, and not a non-empirical paper. Full text appears complete with methods, results (behavioral and fMRI), and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). Given these points, the study meets all required inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making and should be included.

The study uses a delay discounting / intertemporal choice task (delay discounting, Intertemporal Choice Task), which falls outside the review scope. Exclusion criterion E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM — delay discounting/intertemporal choice excluded) is met. The paper does report whole-brain, group-level fMRI activation maps and voxelwise contrasts (hard>easy, hard>no, easy>no), so inclusion criteria I6 (whole-brain group-level maps), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (results reported in text/tables/figures) are satisfied. However I4 (task must be risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM) is not satisfied, and I5 (contrasts appropriate to risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) is not applicable for the review domains. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Excluded under E5: the task is a probabilistic category-learning (weather prediction) nondeclarative learning task rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm as defined by the review. The study does meet several methodological inclusion criteria: I5 (it reports a task > active control contrast: weather prediction > perceptual-motor control), I6 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses using SPM99), I7 (healthy adult participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). However I4 is not met because the experimental task is a category-learning/memory task, not a risky, ambiguity, or perceptual difficulty decision-making task per the meta-analysis definitions. Full text appears complete and was reviewed in detail.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human adults using a probabilistic reinforcement-learning task (uncertain outcomes across 80/20, 70/30, 60/40 pairs). The authors report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with coordinates and cluster-level FWE correction. Crucially, they include parametric contrasts indexing unsigned prediction error (absolute PE) and its overlap with post-error slowing (i.e., brain activity increasing with surprise/uncertainty), which corresponds to a high-uncertainty > low-uncertainty type contrast relevant to ambiguous/risky decision-making. Results are reported as whole-brain maps and coordinates. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria apply (no PET, no ROI-only, not task>rest only, and not only between-group contrasts). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a four-armed bandit gambling task involving decision-making under uncertainty (exploration vs exploitation), which qualifies as risky/ambiguous decision-making. The paper reports a within-task contrast classifying trials as exploratory versus exploitative (a decision-vs-decision comparison). Analyses were conducted at the group level using SPM with whole-brain voxelwise statistics and report whole-brain-corrected activations and peak coordinates (figures and coordinates are provided). Participants are healthy humans. Therefore the study satisfies I4 (fMRI + human decision-making task under uncertainty), I5 (within-task decision contrasts: exploratory > exploitative), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with corrections), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with methods, results, discussion, and coordinates (supplementary methods referenced but core content present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants (n=20) who performed a sequential monetary gambling task involving explicit risky choices (accept vs reject). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM/SnPM) with corrected cluster results and coordinates, and condition contrasts such as accept > reject and parametric modulators (trial outcome, accumulated reward, decision value) that directly compare decision-making conditions (risky vs safe and other within-task contrasts). Full methods, results, and discussion are provided in the text, and whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study with human participants performing a monetary risky decision-making task (gamble choices) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses.
