It includes within-task condition contrasts (frame-consistent vs frame-inconsistent choices) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (unthresholded framing contrast deposited on NeuroVault). Methods, results, and discussion are present and detailed. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for (I4) fMRI during risky decision-making, (I5) at least one condition-vs-condition contrast, (I6) whole-brain group-level maps, (I7) acceptable participant group, and (I8) clearly described whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., contrasts are not against implicit baseline, not PET, not ROI-only, etc.). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (dot-motion coherence), satisfying the review focus. It reports condition-vs-condition contrasts that map onto perceptual-DM contrasts (e.g., low coherence/hard > high coherence/easy; parametric "inverse dependence on coherence" and explicit "low coherence > high coherence" effects). The paper presents voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses with coordinate tables and surface maps (Table 3, figures), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Participants are human and healthy; results are reported in text, figures, and coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not baseline-only contrasts). Full article text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is provided, so fulltext is complete. Hence the study should be INCLUDED.

This study reports human fMRI during a perceptual decision-making task (delayed match-to-category of auditory and tactile frequency sweeps), with condition-vs-condition analyses (up‑sweep vs down‑sweep) and group-level, whole-brain (surface/voxelwise) statistical maps. Methods describe random-effects GLM univariate contrasts and a surface-based whole-brain searchlight MVPA (SVM) decoding up vs down, with cluster-based correction and conjunctions across modalities. Reporting includes full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. These elements satisfy the review’s requirements for fMRI perceptual decision-making, a decision-vs-decision contrast, whole-brain group analyses, and acceptable reporting. No exclusion criteria (e.g., task vs baseline only, PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the article should be included.

This fMRI study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. Instead, one of the tasks is a delay discounting task (intertemporal choice), which is explicitly excluded (E5). Although the study includes whole-brain, group-level task activation maps (satisfying I6), reports results in the main text (I8), and uses an eligible participant group (healthy adults; I7), it does not meet the core inclusion requirements for task type (I4) nor the decision-making-contrast requirement for the allowed DM domains (I5). Therefore it cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human volunteers performing a risky decision-making task (risky £1 vs safer 10p choices) inside the scanner. The authors report whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses identifying neural correlates of decision-related parametric modulators (choice temperature βm and learning rate αm) and contrasts comparing ketamine vs placebo sessions (paired t-tests). These constitute within-task, condition-related task contrasts (trial-wise high vs low decision-related signals) and not task>rest contrasts. Results are reported as whole-brain statistical maps (cluster-corrected) and described in the text. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7 and I8, and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only, and includes within-group whole-brain effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study in which human participants performed a probabilistic (uncertain) decision-making task (trial-and-error probabilistic learning), satisfying the requirement of a risky/ambiguous decision-making paradigm. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with corrected thresholds and peak coordinates (tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Relevant contrasts compare task conditions (high-probability/correct rule vs low-probability/alternative rule) and positive vs negative feedback (within-task condition comparisons), which constitute condition-vs-condition decision-making contrasts. Participants are healthy human subjects (ages 8–22). Results and coordinates are clearly described in the text and figures. Although the fMRI model focused on feedback events rather than choice-onset, the contrasts reflect decision-related conditions (high vs low outcome probability/informative value) and thus meet the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I4, I5, I6, I7, I8. No exclusion criteria applicable.

This is an event-related fMRI study (3T) in healthy human participants performing a game-theory-based risky decision task (iterated game of Chicken) involving risky/aggressive vs safe/reconciliatory choices. The design included within-subject contrasts (selection: risky vs safe) and opponent contrasts (human > computer), and a 2×2 factorial analysis; group-level, whole-brain SPM analyses are reported (whole-brain FDR-corrected results and tables/figures). Full article contains methods, results, and discussion. Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, and task involves risky decision-making rather than purely social/no-uncertainty paradigms). Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision task (reporting painful vs. non-painful detection), meeting the review's perceptual-DM definition. The paper reports condition-wise GLM contrasts (pain vs. no pain during anticipation and stimulation) and whole-brain group-level analyses. It additionally provides whole-brain MVPA results including FWE-corrected voxelwise maps and group-level permutation tests. Participants are human and results are presented in standard whole-brain formats. Therefore inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not resting/connectivity-only; not ROI-only; contrasts are condition-vs-condition, not baseline-only). Full text appears complete.

This study used task-based fMRI in human participants performing an anticipation task with an 'uncertain event' versus 'certain reward' contrast (meets I4 and I5). Participant sample and reporting (healthy adults) are acceptable (meets I7), and peak coordinates are reported (meets I8). However, the reported analyses were restricted to a priori ROIs with small-volume correction (SVC) within those regions; there is no evidence of an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation map. Because the paper reports only ROI-based voxel searches/SVC without whole-brain results, it meets exclusion criterion E6 (studies that report only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the whole-brain meta-analysis.

This fMRI study used the weather prediction probabilistic category-learning task (prediction > perceptual-motor baseline), so it involves decision-making under uncertainty and includes an active task>control contrast (I4 and I5). Participants are human and groups are acceptable (I7), and whole-brain results are described in the text/figures (I8). However, the authors performed an ROI-based SPM factorial ANOVA (analyses were restricted to anatomical ROI masks from the AAL library) and report only ROI-focused activation results. They did not provide an unmasked, whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation map; thus the study reports only ROI analyses and lacks whole-brain voxelwise task maps (violates I6) and meets exclusion E6 (ROI-only results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study investigates social cooperation games (prisoner’s dilemma vs stag hunt) rather than risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is social/moral decision-making, not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise fMRI results reported), I7 (human participant group), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described and reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task per review definitions) and I5 (contrast is PD vs SH, not an accepted risky/ambiguity/perceptual contrast such as “risky>safe” or “ambiguous>non-ambiguous”). Full text appears complete.

This study used fMRI during a monetary reward-learning task emphasizing reward prediction error (RPE) and connectivity (gPPI). However, it did not manipulate or contrast risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making conditions (no contrasts such as “risky > safe”, “ambiguous > non-ambiguous”, or “hard > easy”). The task and reported contrasts focus on RPE/RE/OE and seed-based connectivity; activation analyses were constrained to a reward-related mask rather than presenting an unmasked whole-brain task activation map relevant to risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM. Therefore it does not meet the review’s requirement that the fMRI task be a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm (Exclusion E5). Met inclusion criteria: I7 (participant group acceptable) and I8 (results reported in text/tables/supplement). Not met: I4 (task is not a qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM task), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts), I6 (no unmasked whole-brain task-evoked activation map for a qualifying decision-making contrast).

This is an fMRI study in human participants that explicitly investigates perceptual decision-making under high vs low visibility. It contains a whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise analysis (searchlight decoding and random-effects GLM) comparing decision conditions (low visibility/guessing vs high visibility/perceptual) analogous to hard>easy or low-coherence>high-coherence contrasts. Whole-brain results are reported in the text and figures. Participants meet eligibility, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, connectivity-only, task>rest only) are violated. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in which human participants performed a decision task involving explicit probabilistic outcomes (risk) while deciding whether to transfer a point (altruistic/helping under risk). The paper reports within-task contrasts and factorial comparisons (no self-risk vs high self-risk; low vs high other-need), parametric modulators of self-risk and other-need, and group-level whole-brain GLM results (voxelwise thresholds and cluster FWE correction). The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Although the paradigm has a social/altruistic element, the decision variable is explicit probabilistic risk and thus fits the risky decision-making category. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it does not provide task-evoked, whole-brain fMRI results for a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (the behavioral paradigm is a time-perception/interval estimation task, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and E7 (the neuroimaging data reported are resting-state seed-based connectivity analyses rather than task-evoked whole-brain activation maps). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (human participant group is acceptable; healthy volunteers were tested). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no fMRI scan performed while subjects completed a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no contrast comparing decision-making conditions such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy), and I6 (no group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked statistical map). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion E5 applies: the task is primarily moral/social decision-making (allocating financial harm/help to a charity vs self), which the meta-analysis explicitly excludes. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI results reported with corrected cluster thresholds and coordinates), I7 (healthy adult participants), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/coordinates and described in text). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is framed as social/moral decisions rather than a canonical risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making paradigm targeted by the review), and I5 (no contrast matching the admissible risk/ambiguity/perceptual forms such as "risky > safe" or "high uncertainty > low uncertainty"; condition contrasts focus on self vs charity and gain vs loss rather than risk vs safe or ambiguity contrasts). Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an fMRI study that used a perceptual decision-making task (backward-masked majority function task) manipulating task difficulty/information rate (hard > easy) and exposure time. It reports within-subject condition contrasts (main effects of information entropy, reciprocal of ET, and their interaction) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps with cluster correction. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI contrasts and whole-brain reporting.

This study does not meet the review’s task-type inclusion requirements. Although it reports group-level whole-brain fMRI results (I6) and includes eligible participant groups (I7) and acceptable reporting of whole-brain results (I8), the experimental paradigm is a probabilistic social reinforcement learning task (social reward learning) rather than a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task as defined by the meta-analysis. The paper does not report contrasts of the form required for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy) or within-task risk/ambiguity contrasts; instead analyses focus on reinforcement learning (trial-wise RPE parametric modulation) and social vs non-social feedback. Therefore exclusion criterion E5 (task not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM) is met. Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM), I5 (no qualifying risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrasts). Included criteria met: I6, I7, I8. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (face vs house discrimination near threshold). The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing decision conditions (e.g., HF > FH, FFhc > HHhc), and conducts group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected results, coordinates and figures). Participants are healthy adults. Whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and figures. The full text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is provided. Therefore it meets all relevant inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a risky decision-making task (fMRI-adapted BART) with a clear active vs passive task contrast (active>passive). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FSL FLAME mixed-effects) with cluster-corrected results, tables and figures. All required inclusion criteria are met: I4 (fMRI during risky DM), I5 (task vs active control contrast), I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported). None of the exclusion criteria apply (not a PET, not only ROI or connectivity, contrasts are task vs control not baseline, and contains within-group task effects). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables referenced).

This is an empirical simultaneous EEG-fMRI study in humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion discrimination) with trial-by-trial confidence measures. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results (cluster-corrected) and provides coordinates and statistical maps linking BOLD to parametric contrasts (e.g., confidence-related modulation, EEG-derived high vs. low confidence), satisfying within-task condition comparisons. The methods, results, and discussion are complete in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and contrasts are not only task>rest). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI perceptual decision-making contrasts and whole-brain reporting.

The study is an fMRI investigation of the Trust Game (risky social decision-making) and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (GAME>CONTROL, INVESTOR>CONTROL, TRUSTEE>CONTROL) and coordinates/figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. However, all reported neuroimaging results are between-group comparisons (high-Mach > low-Mach) of the task contrast, and the paper does not present an unmasked, whole-brain within-group/task main effect map (e.g., task>control within a single group or the overall sample). Therefore it falls under exclusion E8 (reports only between-group contrasts with no accompanying unmasked, whole-brain within-group task effect). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision making (object recognition) with human participants. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (repeated-measures mixed-effects ANOVA), contrasts across decision conditions (recognition time TR3–7, comparisons of correct vs. TR8, and static vs. shuffle trials), and presents whole-brain maps and ROI coordinates. These meet inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not only baseline contrasts, not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and it is empirical fMRI data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using a perceptual decision-making task (random-dot motion) with confidence/uncertainty monitoring. It reports within-task contrasts (task trials vs control trials; regressions with decision uncertainty/low-coherence vs high-coherence analog), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (thresholded maps, coordinates referenced). Participants include clinical (schizophrenia) and healthy groups, which are admissible. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (task, fMRI acquisition, GLM), Results (whole-brain maps, ROI and connectivity analyses), and Discussion; no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis (perceptual fMRI task, appropriate contrasts, whole-brain group maps, eligible participants, and acceptable reporting).

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a perceptual decision-making task (3D heading discrimination) with explicit contrasts comparing decision difficulty (EASY vs HARD) across two stimulus manipulations (COH and FOE). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects t-maps, conjunction analysis) are reported with thresholding and coordinates; results are presented in text, figures, and ROI follow-up. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus the study satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8, and violates none of the listed exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI (BOLD) study in healthy human participants performing a gambling/guessing task with uncertainty. It includes task contrasts comparing predicting (guessing) versus reporting (an active control) and difficulty contrasts (suit > colour, hard > easy), analyzed with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM methods and reported as activation foci/figures. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during decision-making task), I5 (decision task > control and hard>easy contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis), I7 (human participants; healthy sample), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not task>rest only, etc.). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study in human participants using a probabilistic monetary-incentive delay task that systematically manipulated outcome probability (20%, 50%, 80%) and magnitude. The paper reports within-task contrasts comparing high- versus low-probability anticipation (PRB: 80 vs 20%) and other decision-related contrasts, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps and Talairach coordinates. These features satisfy the review’s requirements for (I4) an fMRI task involving probabilistic (risky) decision-related processing, (I5) at least one decision-related within-task contrast (high vs low probability), (I6) group-level whole-brain results, (I7) an acceptable participant group (healthy humans), and (I8) reporting of whole-brain results with coordinates and figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy humans that implements a perceptual decision-making task (face/house discrimination with graded difficulty including noise trials) and reports condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., FaceDecision > HouseDecision, parametric contrasts across signal strength/hard>easy manipulations and decision vs instructed responses). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (with cluster correction) including whole-brain reward-network activations; ROI analyses are supplementary but whole-brain results are present in the text/figures. Participants are healthy adults. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study collected whole-brain task-evoked data while human adolescents performed a two-choice facial emotion identification task (perceptual decision-making). It reports a task-versus-active-control contrast (FACE > OVAL), uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (LME with cluster correction), and presents whole-brain results in text/figures/tables. Participants (adolescents with MDD and healthy controls) are acceptable per inclusion rules. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of perceptual decision-making fMRI studies.

This is an fMRI study in human participants that experimentally manipulated decision difficulty and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts relevant to perceptual decision-making. The task required subjects to decide whether a presented probe color matched one or more memorized colors; sample–probe similarity (match, similar non-match, dissimilar non-match) and memory load (1 vs 3 items) produced condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., similarity main effect; high vs low load), which map onto perceptual decision-making contrasts (hard > easy). Analyses were whole-brain SPM random-effects ANOVAs with FDR correction and peak coordinates/tables reported. No exclusion criteria were triggered: contrasts are not baseline-only, the modality is fMRI (not PET), whole-brain results are provided (not ROI-only), and the task fits within the perceptual decision-making domain as argued by the authors. Full text is complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study in humans using a probabilistic decision-making (beads/JTC) task that manipulates uncertainty. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects analyses (with FWE correction) as well as ROI results, and includes contrasts comparing the decision task to an active control task (JTC blocks > control blocks) and event-related contrasts (last fish > preceding fish) that index decision-making under uncertainty. Participants are healthy humans. Results are reported with coordinates and whole-brain statistical inference. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET; not only ROI; not resting-state/connectivity-only; not task>rest only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Hence the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This fMRI study is excluded because it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or canonical perceptual decision-making contrasts (Exclusion E5). The task is a sequence/pattern-learning paradigm where subjects identify gradually revealed images to detect patterns; the reported contrasts (pattern vs no-pattern, RT drops, entropy regressors) index structure learning and uncertainty rather than established perceptual difficulty contrasts (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence) or risk/ambiguity manipulations. The paper does satisfy several inclusion criteria: I6 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported using SnPM and cluster-level FWE correction), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures). However it does not meet I4 (study must be an fMRI of risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined) nor I5 (contains an admissible decision-making contrast such as perceptual hard>easy or equivalent). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED (E5).

This is an empirical fMRI study in human participants using a perceptual decision-making task (dot-motion coherence) with response-signal manipulation. The analyses include condition-wise (motion coherence × duration) GLMs, parametric contrasts for motion coherence (equivalent to 'low coherence > high coherence' / 'hard > easy'), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps (spatial maps normalized to MNI) and ICA-derived whole-brain components. Results are reported at the group level with spatial maps and ROIs; whole-text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I4 (fMRI during perceptual DM), I5 (condition contrasts/parametric comparisons relevant to perceptual DM), I6 (group-level whole-brain analysis), I7 (eligible participant group), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing a gambling task that manipulates risk levels (high- vs low-risk choices) and analyzes outcomes. The methods describe event-related fMRI, voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses and report group- and risk-level contrasts (e.g., high-risk > low-risk for positive outcomes; group×risk interactions). Results include whole-brain coordinates and FWE-corrected statistics. Participant sample (healthy first-degree relatives and controls) is acceptable per the review scope. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (task-based fMRI of risky decision-making; relevant decision contrasts; whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps; acceptable participant group; clear reporting of whole-brain results). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study in healthy humans using a near-threshold pain-detection paradigm (perceptual decision-making). The paper reports within-task condition contrasts (pain vs no pain; high threat vs low threat; interaction contrasts) relevant to perceptual decision-making, and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates. Results include anticipation and stimulation contrasts and whole-brain SPM analyses. The task is a perceptual decision task (detection/classification of stimulus as painful vs nonpainful), satisfying the perceptual-DM domain. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, I8 and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in human participants performing a temporally-extended probabilistic categorization task (perceptual decision-making with uncertainty). The paper reports within-task parametric contrasts (categorical evidence, confidence, and their modulation by urgency — effectively high vs low evidence states) and compares models, with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (SPM analyses, FWER/topological FDR corrections) presented in figures and tables. Participants are healthy adults. The full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not just abstract/metadata). No exclusion criteria (e.g., PET, ROI-only, task>rest-only contrasts, connectivity-only, non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of perceptual decision-making.

This is an fMRI study of intertemporal (delay-discounting) choice in adolescent boys, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Exclusion E5 applies. The study does include a within-task contrast (SS vs LL choices), group-level analyses and whole-brain T-maps are available (satisfying I5, I6, I7, I8), but it fails I4 (task type: not risky/ambiguous/perceptual). Therefore it must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite meeting other technical criteria.

Excluded because the task is a probabilistic reversal learning (reinforcement-learning) paradigm and the reported analyses focus on parametric PE regressors rather than contrasts that match risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making comparisons. Specifically, no contrasts of the form risky>safe, high-uncertainty>low-uncertainty, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy are reported. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses were performed) and I8 (results reported with coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is not clearly a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM task as defined for this meta-analysis) and I5 (no qualifying decision-making condition-vs-condition or task-vs-active-control contrasts are presented). Exclusion criterion invoked: E5 (task does not fit the risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM categories required). Full text appears complete.

The study used fMRI while participants performed perceptual decision-making tasks (spatial comparison and shape comparison), with active baseline target-detection trials and contrasts of interest (spatial comparison > baseline; within- vs between-image comparisons). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise activation and contrasts are reported in the text and figures. Participants were healthy adults. Thus it satisfies the review inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI (I4, I5) and provides whole-brain task-evoked maps at the group level (I6). Reporting in figures/text meets I8, and participant population is acceptable (I7). No exclusion criteria apply (not PET; not resting-state/ROI-only; contrasts are against an active control rather than implicit baseline). Full text appears complete.

Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the task is an ultimatum/dictator social fairness task (decision to punish/accept unfair offers), which is social/economic decision-making, not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (within-task contrasts reported: UG (unfair–fair) and UG−DG contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (fMRI during risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making) — the task does not involve risk/uncertainty or perceptual difficulty as defined by the review. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making.

This fMRI study does not involve a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Participants passively viewed surprised faces during scanning; although faces varied in valence ambiguity, the paradigm assessed emotion perception (valence/arousal) rather than participants making decisions under risk/ambiguity or performing a perceptual difficulty task. Therefore it fails the meta-analysis requirements for (I4) an fMRI decision-making task and (I5) a decision-making contrast (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported) and I7 (healthy human participants). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided). Conclusion: EXCLUDE because the experimental task does not meet the decision-making task requirements (I4, I5 not met).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy human adults performing a perceptual decision-making task (GO/NO-GO). The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (SPM) for parametric contrasts and categorical contrasts across levels of predictive information (within-task condition comparisons), including conjunctions and clusterwise/FWE-corrected inference. Results are reported in the text and supplemental tables/figures. Thus the paper provides whole-brain, task-evoked activation maps for perceptual decision-making contrasts (decision-related parametric and categorical contrasts), meeting the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical concurrent TMS-fMRI study in human participants performing a perceptual decision-making (visual detection) task. The paper reports within-task, decision-related contrasts (misses vs. hits; misses vs. correct rejections) and tests interactions with TMS, which are valid decision-making condition contrasts. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise (permutation-based cluster correction across the whole brain) and results are reported in the text, figures and tables. Participants are healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and is complete for screening. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of perceptual decision-making and no exclusion criteria are met.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E7 — the paper reports ICA-derived networks and component betas (a connectivity/ICA approach) and does not report a standard group-level, whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise activation contrast required for coordinate-based activation meta-analysis. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I4 — fMRI was collected while participants performed a perceptual decision-making (two-choice RT) task; I7 — participants are human healthy adults (young and older) (participant groups acceptable); I8 — MNI coordinates for ICA component maxima are reported. (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I5 — no reported contrast of decision-making conditions (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high, or task>active control); the paper averaged across verbal and numerical blocks rather than presenting within-task condition contrasts; I6 — no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical contrast map (e.g., task>control or condition>condition) is provided. Because I5 and I6 are required and not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (visual object categorization) with condition-vs-condition contrasts (e.g., incongruent > congruent; degraded > intact; interactions of congruency and sensory reliability) and trial-specific RT regressors. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses are reported (voxelwise results with cluster correction). Participants were healthy human volunteers. Results and contrasts are reported in the main text and tables. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and none of the exclusion criteria apply (not PET, not ROI-only, not baseline-only contrasts, not connectivity-only). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study used the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), a canonical risky decision-making paradigm, with participants scanned during task performance. The analyses include within-task, parametrically-modulated contrasts (inflation choice * P(explode); successful inflation * P(explode)) that constitute condition-vs-condition decision-making contrasts, and second-level, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses reporting peak coordinates and cluster statistics. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis criteria for risky decision-making fMRI studies and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It is an fMRI experiment in humans performing a perceptual decision-making task (synchrony/asynchrony judgments) (I4). The authors report condition-versus-control contrasts appropriate for perceptual DM (e.g., asynchrony and synchrony perception > auditory+visual unisensory conditions; i.e., perceptual task > control task) (I5). Whole-brain, group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses are described and reported (SPM second-level one-sample t-tests; activation maps and tables) fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements (I6). Participants are healthy human adults (I7). Results are reported in text/figures/tables with coordinates (I8). No exclusion criteria are met (contrasts are not task>rest only; study is fMRI not PET; whole-brain maps are provided; not ROI-only; not connectivity-only). Therefore I include this study for the meta-analysis.

Full text is complete. Excluded because the fMRI task does not probe risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making: the scanned task was an attentional/conditioned-cue probe (CS+ vs CS−) and the decision-making task (delay discounting) was performed outside the scanner. Therefore this study does not address risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM and fails the meta-analysis inclusion requirements. Exclusion ID met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion IDs met: I6 (reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses), I7 (human participant sample acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables). Inclusion IDs not met: I4 (fMRI was not conducted while participants performed a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task) and I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy was reported for an in-scanner decision task). Given these mismatches, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

EXCLUDED because the study does not provide a qualifying decision-making contrast per the meta-analysis inclusion criteria (I5). Although this is an fMRI study in healthy human participants performing a two-choice perceptual discrimination (color) task (meets I4), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates/figures (meets I6 and I8), and participants qualify (meets I7), the critical requirement I5 is not met: the reported contrasts examine temporal expectancy (good vs bad clock) and accessory (vibration) effects, and task>rest contrasts, but do not include perceptual difficulty or perceptual decision contrasts of the accepted forms (e.g., hard>easy, low coherence>high coherence, or perceptual task>active control) nor ambiguity/risk contrasts (high uncertainty>low uncertainty in the decision dimension). No exclusion criteria (E3–E9) were triggered. Therefore the paper is excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study used fMRI while participants performed a probabilistic reversal learning task involving uncertainty/probabilistic outcomes (i.e., risky decision context). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted: RPE-related parametric modulators were tested with one-sample and two-sample t-tests and whole-brain cluster- and peak-level FWE-corrected results (RPE network) are reported. The paper does not rely solely on ROI analyses and includes within-group task effects in healthy controls and patient subgroups. Although the task is framed as reinforcement/reversal learning rather than explicitly labelled “risky” or “ambiguous,” the probabilistic (80/20) choice structure entails risk/uncertainty and qualifies under the review’s risky/ambiguous decision-making domain. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making as defined by the review (exclusion E5). It instead examines statistical learning and prediction of symbolic sequences (prediction task), and though it contrasts structured vs. random sequences, the task is a learning/prediction paradigm rather than risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM. The paper also emphasizes ICA-based component and connectivity analyses and reports task effects as component β changes rather than providing a standard group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrast map; thus it effectively reports component/ connectivity results without the required voxelwise whole-brain task activation maps, fitting exclusion E7. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (there is a contrast between two task conditions: structured vs. random), I7 (healthy human participants), and I8 (spatial maps/peak coordinates are reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (task is not a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making paradigm), I6 (no clear group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map appropriate for the meta-analysis). Therefore the study should be excluded.

This is an empirical human fMRI study in which participants performed a perceptual decision-making task (animal vs. non-animal detection). The paper reports within-task contrasts (animal > non-animal) and contrasts across complexity conditions, uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME1, cluster-corrected maps), and provides ROI and whole-brain results. Participants are healthy human adults. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (fMRI acquisition and analysis), Results (whole-brain and ROI analyses) and Discussion. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for perceptual decision-making fMRI studies and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI in human participants performing an associative learning task that manipulates outcome uncertainty (precision) and requires trialwise predictions, thereby addressing decision-making under uncertainty/ambiguity. The authors present within-task contrasts comparing precision conditions (high vs low precision) and parametric modulators of unsigned prediction errors across precision levels, which map onto the meta-analysis admissible ambiguous-DM contrasts (high/low uncertainty). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps are reported (whole-brain FWE-corrected results and cluster maps; ROI analyses are supplementary), and results are described in text and figures. Participant samples include healthy controls and clinical groups, which are acceptable per inclusion rules. The provided full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I4, I5, I6, I7, and I8 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain, group-level task analyses of a social learning/advice-taking task (satisfies I4, I6, I7, I8). However, the task centers on social decision-making (inferring adviser fidelity and integrating social advice with probabilistic cues) rather than a pure risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making contrast as defined by the meta-analysis. The review’s exclusion criterion E5 disallows studies whose decision-making task is social (e.g., social learning, advice/gambling framed by social motives). Furthermore, the reported contrasts are model-based social prediction errors and adviser-fidelity/integration effects rather than the domain-specific contrasts required for inclusion (e.g., risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguous, hard>easy). Therefore I5 (required contrast type for risky/ambiguous/perceptual DM) is not met and E5 applies. Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy humans performing a monetary gambling task that manipulates risk. It includes within-task condition contrasts relevant to risky decision-making (e.g., high-risk wins > low-risk wins; a risk-choice contrast modeling linear increase with risk magnitude), satisfying the required risky-DM contrast forms. Analyses are group-level, voxelwise, whole-brain (SPM8 second-level ANOVAs) with reported whole-brain clusters and ROI-corrected results, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. Participants are healthy adults. Results are presented in tables and figures. No exclusion criteria apply: contrasts are condition-versus-condition (not only baseline), modality is fMRI (not PET), task is a risky decision-making paradigm (not excluded DM types), whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), and the paper reports task activations rather than only connectivity or between-group-only contrasts. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI risky decision-making.

This is an fMRI study in healthy human participants that acquired whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation maps while participants performed a prediction task based on perceptual sequences. The study includes condition contrasts of interest (structured vs. random sequences; i.e., decision/perceptual task vs. an active control sequence condition), reports whole-brain voxelwise GLM results and corrected statistical maps, and provides coordinates/figures. The task constitutes a perceptual decision-making paradigm under uncertainty (prediction of next stimulus), fitting the review’s perceptual-DM domain. No exclusion criteria are met (not PET, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not task>baseline only, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This study is excluded because its fMRI tasks are cue-reactivity and response-inhibition, not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making tasks (Exclusion E5). Additionally, the imaging analysis was restricted to an ROI mask rather than a whole-brain task activation map, meeting Exclusion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (human participant group qualifies) and I8 (whole-brain results may be reported in tables/coordinates — the paper reports activation coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI was not conducted during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no eligible decision-making contrasts of the accepted forms such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy), and I6 (no unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map reported). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. It uses fMRI during an olfactory intensity-rating task combined with a memory (cognitive load) manipulation. Exclusion criterion E5 applies: the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task. Met inclusion criteria: I6 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported), I7 (healthy adult participants qualify), and I8 (whole-brain results and cluster/coordinate information are described). Not met inclusion criteria: I4 (no risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task performed during fMRI) and I5 (no decision-making contrast such as risky>safe, ambiguous>non-ambiguous, or hard>easy). Full text appears complete and sufficient to determine eligibility.

This study conducted 3T fMRI while participants performed two-arm bandit decision-making tasks with probabilistic rewards and changing reward probabilities (social: faces smiling; non-social: houses open/locked). The fMRI analyses modeled volatility (uncertainty), prediction errors, and value expectation and tested whole-brain voxelwise encodings, reporting cluster coordinates and t-values (group-level whole-brain results). Thus it satisfies: I4 (fMRI during decision-making task under uncertainty), I5 (parametric contrasts/analyses of uncertainty/volatility and decision-related computations consistent with ambiguous/risky decision-making contrasts), I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates), I7 (participant groups acceptable), and I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not PET, does not report only ROI or connectivity, and includes within-task computational modulators rather than only task>rest contrasts. Although one task was social, a non-social bandit was also acquired and modeled, and volatility/uncertainty-related regressors map onto ambiguous/risky DM constructs. Therefore include.

Excluded because the study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making (E5). This is a value-based food vs. nonfood purchasing task (BDM auction) and thus falls outside the meta-analysis domains. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported with second-level GLMs and coordinate tables/figures), I7 (human healthy participants), I8 (whole-brain results and coordinates are clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (fMRI was not conducted during a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (the reported contrasts compare food vs nonfood valuation and sleep states rather than the accepted risky/ambiguous/perceptual contrast forms required by the review). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study must be excluded under E5.

This fMRI study used a visual food perception paradigm (Food > Non-Food) in healthy participants and reports group-level task effects. However, it does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making: the task is passive viewing with attention targets and tastiness ratings, not a risky/ambiguous choice or a perceptual decision manipulation (e.g., hard>easy, low vs high coherence). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I4 and I5. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level task-evoked analysis/second-level random-effects contrasts were generated and whole-brain effects are reported/supplemented), I7 (participant group acceptable: healthy adults), and I8 (results reported in text/figures/supplement). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Hence the study is excluded from the meta-analysis focused on risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making.

This study uses an fMRI trust game (human vs computer counterparts) that is a social decision-making task focused on betrayal aversion. The review’s exclusion criterion E5 explicitly excludes moral or social decision-making tasks. Although the paper reports whole-brain, group-level SPM results and contrasts that include a risky > safe style comparison (trusting > not trusting) and provides coordinate tables, the task is fundamentally social/trust-based rather than the non-social risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making targeted by the meta-analysis. Therefore it fails the inclusion requirement about task domain (I4) and must be excluded under E5.

Exclusion summary: E5 applies — the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making paradigm but a visuomotor/sequence-statistics finger-tapping task assessing entropy and surprise in stimulus/action sequences. Included criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise fMRI analyses were conducted and reported), I7 (healthy adult participants were tested), I8 (whole-brain results are clearly described in the text and supplementary material). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (the task is not a risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making task), I5 (there is no eligible risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision contrast of the forms required by the review; the main contrast is choice vs specified action related to sequence regularity, not risk/ambiguity/perceptual difficulty). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be excluded under E5.

This fMRI study measured neural responses during processing of uncertain versus certain cues (UNC vs CNC and UNC vs CFC), providing within-task contrasts that match ambiguous decision-making comparisons (ambiguous > non-ambiguous). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects maps (FDR-corrected) and results are reported voxelwise. Participants are human (healthy university sample). The task examines uncertainty processing during cue encoding, which fits the review’s ambiguous-DM domain. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for ambiguous decision-making fMRI contrasts and whole-brain reporting.

This study reports an fMRI experiment in which human participants performed a risky decision-making task (accept/reject mixed gambles) while scanned; it includes within-task contrasts targeting neural correlates of loss aversion (parametric modulators for gains and losses and neural loss-aversion contrasts) and between-task contrasts (CONTINGENT vs RANDOM) at the group-level using SPM8 random-effects whole-brain analyses with reported stereotaxic coordinates and corrected cluster statistics. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. All required inclusion criteria are met (I4, I5, I6, I7, I8) and no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the paper should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of risky decision-making.

Excluded because the study does not investigate risky, ambiguous, or perceptual decision-making. Exclusion criteria met: E5 (decision-making task is not risky, ambiguous, or perceptual DM). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported), I7 (healthy human participant sample), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I4 (fMRI during a risky/ambiguous/perceptual decision-making task), I5 (no qualifying decision-making contrasts such as risky>safe, ambiguity>non-ambiguity, or hard>easy). Full text appears complete.
